title: From efficiency to redesign: different trajectories to reduce pesticide use in French vineyards
Estimating malaria burden in sub-Saharan Africa under intervention disruption using satellite-derived representations
abstractText: Abstract Malaria remains a leading cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide, particularly in sub-Saharan Africa. Stalled progress and funding constraints raise important questions about the dependence of current malaria burden on sustained intervention coverage. Here, we estimate malaria transmission potential under a low-intervention scenario where major malaria interventions are withdrawn while broader ecological and demographic conditions remain constant. We develop a contrastive representation-learning framework applied to 30-m Landsat 8 satellite imagery, integrating the resulting environmental representations within a Bayesian hierarchical model. This approach improves predictive accuracy over existing covariate-based malaria mapping methods. Using contemporary Global Burden of Disease 2024 population estimates, we estimate an annual malaria burden of 422 (275-582) million cases across sub-Saharan Africa, representing a 131% increase relative to current estimates. These findings quantify the structural vulnerability of malaria control gains across sub-Saharan Africa and reveal where intervention disruption could have the greatest impact.

title: DeepChem-DEL: An Open-Source Framework for Reproducible DEL Modeling and Benchmarking
abstractText: Abstract DNA-encoded libraries (DELs) allow screening of extremely large chemical spaces by tagging compounds with DNA barcodes. Machine learning (ML) techniques have enabled the extraction of meaningful chemical patterns from noisy, target-specific DEL binding data. However, existing tools for DEL machine learning (DEL-ML) remain fragmented, which limits systematic construction and reproducibility of modeling pipelines. Moreover, this fragmentation hinders integration of new models, such as chemical foundation models, into DEL workflows alongside classical approaches. To address these challenges in DEL modeling, we introduce DeepChem-DEL, an open-source suite of reproducible ML workflows for DEL modeling built on the DeepChem ecosystem. DeepChem-DEL integrates (i) a configurable denoising pipeline with (ii) modular DeepChem workflows for enrichment prediction, hit identification, and benchmarking across diverse model classes, including chemical foundation models enabled through extensions to the open-source ChemBERTa-3 framework. We evaluate DeepChem-DEL on the KinDEL and BELKA data sets, reproducing key baselines and enabling direct comparison across model classes. Our experiments demonstrate that leveraging chemical foundation models yields performance competitive with, and in several cases exceeding, previously explored approaches such as graph convolutional networks and random forest models. Together, these results demonstrate that DeepChem-DEL is a scalable and extensible platform for DEL-ML, while highlighting the potential of chemical foundation models for improved DEL modeling and prioritization.

title: Regulation of Irpex lacteus-mediated bioconversion of Caragana korshinskii lignocellulose by nitrogen source forms: transcriptomics evidence from lignocellulose degradation to protein enrichment
abstractText: Caragana korshinskii is a typical woody biomass resource. Irpex lacteus exhibits strong potential for efficient lignocellulose degradation, yet its metabolic performance may vary with nitrogen availability. This study investigated the effects of organic nitrogen, inorganic nitrogen and nitrogen addition level on I. lacteus-mediated degradation of C. korshinskii lignocellulose and protein enrichment, as well as the transcriptional mechanisms underlying nitrogen metabolism during bioconversion. The results showed that, compared with inorganic nitrogen sources, organic nitrogen at a 1.0% nitrogen addition level significantly enhanced lignin degradation and protein enrichment, achieving a lignin degradation rate of 34.58% and true protein increasing of 40.48%. Transcriptomic analysis further revealed organic nitrogen addition can significant enrichment of metabolic pathways related to fatty acids, amino acids, and carbohydrates, along with upregulation of genes encoding manganese peroxidase and those involved in amino acid transport and metabolism. These findings demonstrate that nitrogen source forms regulate I. lacteus nitrogen metabolism, thereby influencing the transcriptional expression and extracellular secretion of lignocellulose-degrading enzymes. This study provides metabolic and genetic insights into optimizing lignocellulose bioconversion efficiency through nitrogen regulation.

title: Roxadustat for treatment of suspected erythropoietin(EPO)-induced pure red cell aplasia in a hemodialysis patient: a case report
abstractText: Abstract Anemia is a prevalent complication in patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD), particularly those undergoing dialysis. Recombinant human erythropoietin (rhEPO) is widely administered to patients both on and off dialysis to manage this anemia. However, despite an initial favorable therapeutic response, a sudden and unexplained decline in hemoglobin levels (Hb) often prompts the need for further diagnostic evaluation. In this context, we report a clinical case involving a 48-year-old male patient who had been undergoing hemodialysis (HD) for two years. During the course of his rhEPO treatment regimen, he developed pure red cell aplasia (PRCA), a rare but serious adverse reaction. Upon recognition of this complication, the administration of rhEPO was promptly discontinued, and the patient was initiated on roxarestat therapy. Remarkably, following nine months of continuous roxarestat treatment, the patient experienced a significant and sustained increase in his Hb levels. This clinical outcome underscores the importance of prompt diagnosis and intervention in cases of EPO-induced PRCA. Furthermore, our findings suggest that roxarestat may serve as a viable and effective therapeutic option for patients with EPO-induced PRCA, potentially obviating the need for immunosuppressive therapy and its associated risks.

title: Chromosome-level assembly and population-scale genomics in an intensively monitored wild bird, the Seychelles warbler
abstractText: Abstract Understanding evolutionary processes is greatly facilitated by high-quality data on genetic variation. We report the development of a genomic toolkit for a recently bottlenecked, long-term studied species, the Seychelles warbler (Ptimerl dezil; Acrocephalus sechellensis). This toolkit comprises a reference genome assembled into 31 chromosomes, together with functional annotations and reference-panel-free imputation of whole-genome sequences from 1,935 individuals. The genomic data have been used to assign the sequenced individuals into a genetic pedigree. Individual genomic data are associated with a suite of phenotypic metadata, amassed from three decades of fieldwork in this closed, long-term monitored population. We compared sex and parentage assigned using the genomic data with the previously recorded sex and parentage metadata to identify and correct 41 sample DNA samples labelled with the wrong identity. This population resource enables a wide range of analyses, that include, but are not limited to phylogenetics, metabarcoding, recombination rates, linkage patterns, adaptation, heritability, demographic history, selection, and inbreeding estimates. We wish to encourage interest from researchers seeking to collaborate on future analyses and data collection. Overall, our methods demonstrate the potential of next generation sequencing and statistical tools to provide dense genomic datasets at large sample sizes for wild populations.

title: Bacillus cereus PHB CMST1: a potential Halophilic Bacterium for cost-effective and sustainable production of polyhydroxyalkanoates
abstractText: Abstract Bacteria can spontaneously produce polyhydroxyalkanoate (PHA), a thermoplastic and biodegradable substance. PHA is the best polymer substitute for plastic made from petrochemicals. In this investigation, we isolated sixteen bacterial strains from brine and sediment samples collected from a solar salt works facility. Among the sixteen bacterial strains screened for polyhydroxyalkanoate (PHA) production, two strains, Z6 and Z9, exhibited promising results based on Sudan Black B and Nile Blue A staining. Subsequent morphological, biochemical, and molecular characterization identified strain Z9 as Bacillus cereus PHB CMST1 through 16S rRNA sequencing, which demonstrated superior PHA production compared to the other strain. To optimize PHA production, we employed a one-factor-at-a-time (OFAT) methodology, revealing optimal conditions of 35°C, pH 7, 2% salinity, and a 3-day incubation period, utilizing wheat bran as the carbon source and urea as the nitrogen source. Further optimization using Response Surface Methodology-Central Composite Design (RSM-CCD) indicated that B. cereus strain PHB CMST1 requires 5% wheat bran and 2% urea for enhanced PHA synthesis. The yellowish-green dots in the thin layer chromatography (TLC) plate indicated the presence of PHA. FT-IR analysis confirmed that, 𝛽-glycosidic linkages between the sugar monomers were found. The derivatives of polyhydroxybutyric acid confirmed the monomeric polymer by GC-MS analysis. PHA's XRD study showed wide peaks at 20° and 43°, indicating that the PHA had a semi-crystalline structure. Bacillus cereus shows considerable promise for cost-effective and large-scale production of PHA bioplastics, utilizing wheat bran as a non-expensive carbon source.

title: Post-processing strategies for generative design outcomes in a UAV tail boom
abstractText: Abstract Generative design produces structurally efficient but organically shaped geometries that require post-processing before Fused Deposition Modeling (FDM) manufacturing. This paper compares two post-processing strategies applied to the same generative design outcome for an Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) tail boom: a complex variant faithful to the raw topology, and a simplified variant with symmetric arms, self-supporting geometry, and uniform cross-sections oriented toward FDM manufacturability. Both variants were evaluated using linear static and buckling finite element analysis underidentical loading conditions. Scaled prototypes of the simplified variant were FDM-printed at two infill configurations and physically load-tested. The manufacturing-oriented simplification reduced both mass and print time while eliminating support structures; peak stress remained well below the material limit. FEA-predicted stress concentrations correlated with observed fracture locations in physical tests. For lightly loaded polymer FDM structures, these results suggest that manufacturing-oriented simplification of generative design outcomes incurs a negligible structural penalty while improving printability and reducing production cost.

title: Axisymmetric membrane shapes in the Willmore and Helfrich models: First integrals and a hyperbolic formulation
abstractText: The equilibrium shapes of fluid lipid membranes are governed by nonlinear differential equations derived from the Helfrich bending energy. In the tensionless, pressure-free and zero-spontaneous-curvature limit, the governing equation reduces to the Willmore equation. We show that the combination of the Zheng–Liu and Langer–Singer first integrals reduces the third-order axisymmetric Willmore equation to a first-order ordinary differential equation. This formulation recovers the sphere, axisymmetric minimal surfaces, and the Clifford torus as special cases, while organizing the local solution space according to two integration constants. For nonzero spontaneous curvature, the axisymmetric Helfrich functional is reformulated as the energy of an inhomogeneous hyperbolic elastica with a preferred curvature proportional to the distance from the axis. This formulation identifies a constant-mean-curvature branch and a logarithmic branch associated with a biconcave disk profile. The resulting exact relations provide analytical constraints and benchmark solutions for configurations of axisymmetric vesicles and biomembranes.

title: Nocturnal Respiratory Rate and Variability Predict Long-Term Mortality in Stable Outpatients With Cardiovascular Risk Factors
abstractText: Abstract Background Respiratory rate (RR) predicts short-term mortality in acute care settings, yet its prognostic significance in clinically stable outpatients remains poorly defined. Objectives To determine whether the median and variability of nocturnal respiratory rate (NRR) are independently associated with long-term cardiovascular and all-cause mortality in outpatients with cardiovascular disease. Methods We analyzed overnight chest belt waveforms from elective polysomnography in 5,679 older adults with cardiovascular disease enrolled in the Sleep Heart Health Study (SHHS). NRR was quantified at 30-second resolution, and per-subject median NRR and within-night variability (standard deviation) were derived. Kaplan-Meier survival analysis and Cox proportional hazards models were used to evaluate associations with cardiovascular and all-cause mortality over 3-year and 15-year follow-up periods, adjusting for demographic characteristics, cardiopulmonary comorbidities, and sleep apnea severity. Results Higher median NRR and greater NRR variability were each associated with increased cardiovascular and all-cause mortality. Combining these metrics identified a high-risk group characterized by high median and high variability of NRR, with nearly five-fold higher 3-year all-cause mortality compared with a low-risk group (unadjusted HR: 2.61; 95% CI: 1.65, 4.14; p <0.001; adjusted HR: 2.15; 95% CI: 1.30, 3.55; p =0.003). Conclusions Both the baseline level and variability of NRR independently predict morttality in clinically stable outpatients with cardiovascular disease. Densely profiled NRR represents a promising, underutilized biomarker for long-term risk stratification. Condensed Abstract Nocturnal respiratory rate (NRR) is an underutilized biomarker whose prognostic significance in stable cardiovascular outpatients is unknown. In 5,679 participants from the Sleep Heart Health Study, median NRR and within-night variability derived from overnight polysomnography independently predicted cardiovascular and all-cause mortality. Stratification based on these metrics identified a high-risk group with nearly five-fold higher 3-year mortality compared with a low-risk group (adjusted HR: 2.15; 95% CI: 1.30-3.55; p =0.003).

title: Chronic tophaceous gout with suspected axial and atypical joint involvement in the setting of chronic kidney disease: a case series
abstractText: Abstract Gout is a crystal-induced arthritis caused by the deposition of monosodium urate crystals and is one of the most common inflammatory arthritides worldwide. In patients with long-standing hyperuricemia, particularly those with chronic kidney disease, gout may progress to chronic tophaceous disease, characterised by progressive joint destruction and extra-articular crystal deposition. Although gout classically affects the peripheral joints of the feet, advanced disease may result in extensive erosive changes involving the tarsometatarsal and metatarsophalangeal joints, leading to deformity and functional impairment. Multisite involvement, including destructive peripheral joint disease, spinal lesions involving the axial skeleton, and atypical locations such as the shoulder, is uncommon and may mimic other inflammatory, infective, or degenerative musculoskeletal disorders, resulting in diagnostic delay and therapeutic challenges. We present a case series of two patients with advanced chronic tophaceous gout demonstrating atypical and axial involvement.

title: Perceived school support and self-reported digital civic responsibility among vocational health professions students in China: a cross-sectional study
abstractText: Abstract Background Institutional conditions associated with responsible digital participation remain underexamined in health professions education. This study estimated the covariation between perceived school support and self-reported digital civic responsibility among vocational health professions students in China. Methods A cross-sectional electronic survey was administered at one vocational health professions college in Jiangsu Province in 2026. The primary exposure was a five-item perceived school support score; the outcome was a ten-item digital civic responsibility score. Standardized ordinary least-squares regression with HC3 robust standard errors adjusted for prespecified background and social-media-use characteristics. Sex and academic program were excluded from the primary model because of extreme category imbalance (90.5% women; 52.9% nursing students). Ordinal measurement screening, Harman diagnostics, and sensitivity analyses assessed construct separation, same-source measurement, eligibility, use-hours coding, and plausible class clustering. Results The dataset included 840 respondents (mean age 19.41 years; 90.5% women). School support and responsibility were strongly correlated (Spearman’s ρ = 0.771). Their adjusted association was large (standardized β = 0.745, 95% confidence interval 0.680–0.810; p < 0.001; R²=0.638), remained similar after the eligibility restriction (β = 0.750) and categorical coding of use time (β = 0.747), and attenuated after literacy adjustment (β = 0.314). The heterotrait–monotrait ratio was 0.853, exceeding the stringent 0.85 threshold; discriminant validity was not established under that criterion (latent correlation 0.842). The first unrotated component explained 50.3% of variance across all 59 Likert items and 72.4% across the 15 focal items. Conclusions Students who rated school support more favorably also rated their digital civic responsibility more favorably. Same-source measurement, a dominant general response factor, and unestablished discriminant validity could substantially inflate this association; it should not be interpreted as an independent or causal effect. The result is hypothesis-generating and supports prospective, multi-source evaluation.

title: Ultralight 110-mm-aperture planar liquid-crystal diffractive lens for photon-counting LiDAR
abstractText: Lightweight large-aperture receiving optics are crucial for photon-starved long-range active imaging. Here, we demonstrate a 110-mm-aperture ultralight planar liquid-crystal diffractive lens for photon-counting LiDAR. For this lightweight diffractive receiving architecture, we analyze how wavefront aberration, target depolarization, and wavelength-dependent defocus of the Pancharatnam–Berry-phase liquid-crystal lens affect multimode-fiber coupling at the receiver level. The results reveal aberration-tolerant coupling, depolarization-dominated useful-signal loss, and an additional spatial-spectral filtering response enabled by chromatic defocus and finite-core fiber coupling. A coaxial photon-counting LiDAR prototype improves indoor signal-to-background ratio and depth stability and achieves 1.5-km three-dimensional imaging under daytime field conditions. These results provide a scalable planar-optics route toward lightweight, high-sensitivity photon-counting LiDAR for long-range active imaging.

Active cancellation method of window noise in asymmetric buffer cavity based on synergistic modulation of acoustic impedance and phase
abstractText: To mitigate the effect of window thermal noise on detection sensitivity in a photoacoustic cell, an active cancellation method for window noise in an asymmetric buffer cavity is proposed. This method is based on the collaborative modulation of acoustic impedance and phase. A phase balance equation and a noise amplitude balance equation are established for acoustic wave interference cancellation. Theoretical derivation reveals the quantitative relationship between the dimensions of the asymmetric buffer cavity and the degree of noise suppression. Active cancellation of window thermal noise at the midpoint of the resonant cavity is thus achieved. Based on this principle, an asymmetric internal differential photoacoustic cell was designed. Numerical simulations showed that at 1656 Hz, the noise was reduced to 29.3% of that of the conventional photoacoustic cell, and the signal-to-noise ratio improved by a factor of 3.3. Experimental results from methane detection using this asymmetric internal differential photoacoustic cell show that window noise is reduced to 30.3% of that in conventional design, and the signal-to-noise ratio increases by a factor of 2.5. This method provides a new noise suppression approach for high-precision photoacoustic sensing.

title: Polarization-independent quasi-bound states in the continuum in a symmetry-reduced plasmonic metasurface for biosensing
abstractText: Bound states in the continuum (BICs) in plasmonic metasurfaces provide an attractive platform for refractive-index-based biosensing because of their high quality ( Q ) factors and strong electromagnetic field confinement. However, most plasmonic quasi-BICs (qBICs) are realized via in-plane symmetry breaking, which typically introduces pronounced polarization sensitivity and thus complicates optical interrogation and device integration. Here, a polarization-independent strategy for exciting a plasmonic qBIC is demonstrated using a metallic binary metasurface composed of dual-sized Au nanodisks with different diameters. The resulting binary metasurface supports a narrowband qBIC mode with enhanced near-field confinement and reduced radiative loss. Compared with conventional plasmonic resonances, this mode exhibits significantly improved sensitivity to perturbations in the surrounding dielectric environment, yielding a bulk refractive-index sensitivity of 571.2 nm/RIU. When implemented as a biosensor, the metasurface further enables highly sensitive detection of concanavalin A (Con A), with a limit of detection as low as 1.287 nM. These results establish polarization-independent plasmonic qBIC as a practical route toward high-performance metasurface biosensors with high sensitivity, low detection limit, and ease of integration.

title: Fiber-optic photoacoustic dual-gas sensor with multi-frequency cooperative noise suppression and cross-orthogonal multiple-reflection excitation enhancement
abstractText: A fiber-optic photoacoustic gas sensor (FOPAS) that incorporates multi-frequency cooperative noise suppression and cross-orthogonal multiple-reflection enhanced excitation is proposed for simultaneous detection of trace dual-component gases. The optimized composite buffer chambers effectively suppress the acoustic noise at two independent resonance frequencies corresponding to the resonance tube and the cantilever. Compared with conventional cylindrical buffer chambers, the designed composite structure reduces the background signal by 23% and the noise level by 20%. The cross-orthogonal multi-reflection optical structure enables two excitation lasers to be individually coupled into separate fiber collimators and simultaneously injected into the sensor. This overcomes the inherent channel spacing limitations of conventional wavelength division multiplexers (WDMs) while avoiding wavelength-selective optical losses. The resonance tube and the cantilever exhibit independent resonance peaks at 938 Hz and 1216 Hz, respectively. Dual-gas signals are naturally decoupled by employing two independent resonance acoustic fields, whereby acoustic crosstalk between the channels and cross-interference between the target gases are rendered negligible. The minimum detection limits (MDLs) are 8.2 ppb for CO and 3.1 ppb for H 2 S. The corresponding normalized noise equivalent absorption (NNEA) coefficients are 2.04×10 −10 W cm −1 Hz −1/2 for CO and 2.49×10 −10 W cm −1 Hz −1/2 for H 2 S.

title: Tunable on-chip hybrid terahertz emitter combining a spintronic and a photoconductive switch
abstractText: We demonstrate a monolithic terahertz (THz) emitter that combines a GaAs photoconductive antenna (PCA) with a spintronic THz emitter (STE). A single laser can efficiently excite both THz emitters, with the two channels operating separately controllable. Magnetic control of the STE occurs via the inverse spin Hall effect, and electrical tuning of the PCA occurs through bias voltage. Their different wavelength responses allow coherent vector superposition of the slightly delayed pulses, enabling switchable symmetric or asymmetric waveforms and linear or elliptical polarization without modulators. This hybrid emitter achieves a 14.26-fold electric field strength enhancement at 0.25 THz compared with the STE alone. The on-chip hybrid THz emitter-based THz dual-comb spectroscopy exhibits a comb linewidth of 0.98 MHz, paving a pathway toward multifunctional THz technologies.

title: Optically transparent, water-reconfigurable spin-multiplexed metasurface for multispectral camouflage
abstractText: This paper proposes a design methodology for a reconfigurable multispectral camouflage metasurface that integrates microwave stealth, optical transparency, and infrared stealth. The metasurface achieves tunable electromagnetic responses through a water-based reconfiguration mechanism, while optical transparency and infrared stealth are realized using transparent materials and optimized structural patterning. As a proof of concept, the proposed metasurface was validated through numerical simulation, fabrication, and experimental characterization. Both simulated and experimental results confirm a radar cross section reduction exceeding 10 dB over a wide frequency band under left-handed circularly polarized incidence. Under right-handed circularly polarized incidence, the metasurface reproduces a metallic dihedral corner-like scattering response. Water loading modifies the effective impedance of the metasurface, driving a transition from spin-multiplexed wavefront control to a metallic-like scattering state, thereby enabling reconfigurable electromagnetic camouflage and target mimicry. In addition, the metasurface maintains optical transparency and low infrared emissivity. Enabled by its water-based reconfigurability and multispectral stealth capability, it shows strong potential for advanced camouflage applications.

title: Association of Life's Essential 8 with Risk of ESKD in the UK Biobank Study
abstractText: KEY POINTS: Lower Life's Essential 8 scores suggestive of poorer cardiovascular health were associated with a higher risk of incident ESKD. Associations were stronger for the biological than the behavioral subscale; smoking, physical activity, BP, and glucose were key factors. Our findings support the relevance of modifiable Life's Essential 8 health behaviors and clinical indicators as potential targets for preventive kidney health strategy. BACKGROUND: Life's Essential 8 (LE8) is a comprehensive cardiovascular health metric integrating 8 behavioral and biological factors and has been associated with cardiovascular disease risk. However, evidence linking LE8 to ESKD is lacking. METHODS: We analyzed the UK Biobank data prospectively on participants who were free of ESKD at baseline. The LE8 score, calculated as the unweighted average of 8 components (range, 0-100), was categorized as low (0-49), moderate (50-79), and high (80-100), with higher scores indicating more favorable health status. The primary outcome was incident ESKD, defined as needing KRT or reaching CKD stage G5. We used Cox proportional hazards models to estimate hazard ratios (HRs) for incident ESKD, separately for LE8 categories and for continuous LE8 scores, with nonlinear associations assessed using restricted cubic splines. We also estimated population-attributable fractions for nonoptimal LE8 and its subscales and components. RESULTS: Among 276,494 participants (mean [SD] age 56 [8] years; 48% male; 95% White), 455 incident ESKD events occurred over a median follow-up of 14.1 years. In fully adjusted Cox models, each 10-point decrement in LE8 score was associated with higher ESKD risk (HR, 1.47; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.34 to 1.60). Compared with high LE8, moderate LE8 was associated with a 2.1-fold higher risk of incident ESKD (HR, 2.11; 95% CI, 1.39 to 3.21), and low LE8 was associated with a more than five-fold higher risk (HR, 5.57; 95% CI, 3.42 to 9.07). Subscale analyses showed similar patterns. Restricted cubic splines analysis suggested nonlinear associations for overall LE8 and the biological subscale, with steeper risk gradients at lower scores. BP, blood glucose, physical activity, and smoking had statistically significant estimated population-attributable fractions for incident ESKD, with the largest fractions observed for BP and blood glucose. CONCLUSIONS: In this large prospective cohort, lower LE8 scores were associated with a higher risk of incident ESKD. These findings highlight the potential relevance of LE8-guided improvement in behavioral and biological factors for ESKD prevention.

title: Exact reconstruction of a hyperbolic-cosine bounce in f(G,T) gravity: Cosmography, energy conditions and matter content
abstractText: Standard big-bang cosmology, traced backward in time, ends in an initial singularity. This problem motivates bouncing scenarios, in which the Universe contracts to a finite minimum size and then expands again smoothly. We investigate whether such a non-singular bounce can be realized in [Formula: see text] gravity, where the gravitational Lagrangian depends on the Gauss–Bonnet invariant G and on the trace T of the energy-momentum tensor. On a flat FLRW background, we derive the effective density and pressure of the theory, the corresponding energy conditions, and the modified matter conservation law, and we show how the cosmographic parameters enter the energy conditions. For the exact bounce [Formula: see text], the field equations give [Formula: see text], independently of the model, so the effective null energy condition is necessarily violated. We then reconstruct [Formula: see text] directly from this background. The modified Friedmann equation becomes a linear second-order differential equation, which we solve in closed form in vacuum and for a linear coupling [Formula: see text] to dust that obeys the modified conservation law. The resulting Lagrangian makes the bounce an exact solution of both Friedmann equations, while the dust itself satisfies all matter energy conditions. For three viable [Formula: see text] models combined with a power of the trace, we determine the matter content required by the bounce and scan the parameter space for solutions in which this matter satisfies the weak energy condition during the whole evolution. BEYOND THE FRAGRANCE: CULTURAL STORYTELLING, SACRED-IMAGE SENSITIVITY, AND CONSUMER RESPONSES TO INCENSE PACKAGING—A MIXED-METHODS STUDY OF CYCLE PURE AGARBATTI IN INDIA
abstractText: What happens when a heritage incense brand uses cultural stories on packaging that consumers will ultimately discard? This mixed-methods study examines how consumers and cultural stakeholders respond to proposed culture-led packaging for Cycle Pure Agarbatti in India. The research combines a reported overall survey sample of 160 respondents with four regional focus-group cohorts and depth interviews involving consumers, ritual practitioners, temple priests and an academic informant. Survey responses indicate broad initial interest in regionally themed packs, storytelling and limited editions, alongside stated willingness among some respondents to pay a modest premium. The qualitative accounts complicate this enthusiasm. Participants distinguish routine household purchases from gifting occasions and repeatedly emphasize fragrance quality, affordability, authentic representation and the handling of sacred imagery after use. The most consequential tension arises when reverential images are placed on disposable cartons. Integrating both strands, the paper proposes a Cultural Representation–Responsibility–Response framework for designing and testing culturally responsible packaging. Findings are exploratory: varying item-level response counts, non-representative sampling and qualitative summaries limit statistical generalization. The study contributes a context-sensitive account of cultural packaging in an everyday worship-adjacent product category and identifies practical questions for responsible brand experimentation.

abstractText: Program Kuliah Kerja Nyata (KKN) Tematik di Desa Cinta Rakyat, Kecamatan Percut Sei Tuan, Kabupaten Deli Serdang, difokuskan pada dua kegiatan utama, yaitu sosialisasi pencegahan Infeksi Saluran Pernapasan Akut (ISPA) dan survei serta edukasi terkait Program Makan Bergizi Gratis (MBG). Sosialisasi ISPA dilakukan melalui penyuluhan di sekolah dan kunjungan door-to-door kepada masyarakat. Kegiatan ini mendapatkan antusiasme warga mengenai faktor risiko ISPA, seperti kebiasaan merokok di dalam rumah, ventilasi yang buruk, serta rendahnya kesadaran perilaku hidup bersih. Survei MBG dilaksanakan pada empat kelompok sasaran, yaitu siswa SD Negeri 101780, siswa SD Negeri 104028, balita, ibu hamil, dan ibu menyusui. Hasil survei menunjukkan bahwa program MBG memberikan manfaat nyata berupa peningkatan energi, dukungan nutrisi, dan meringankan beban ekonomi keluarga. Namun, hambatan yang ditemui meliputi distribusi yang belum merata, kualitas makanan yang tidak selalu terjaga, serta respon masyarakat yang beragam. Secara keseluruhan, kegiatan KKN ini memperlihatkan pentingnya edukasi kesehatan berbasis masyarakat dan evaluasi program pemerintah agar pelaksanaannya lebih optimal dan berkelanjutan

title: Asteroseismology of blue straggler stars in ω Centauri. Stellar collisions as a possible formation scenario
abstractText: Blue stragglers are intriguing stars that appear more massive and younger than expected from single-star evolution, yet their evolutionary histories remain elusive because of multiple possible formation channels. A promising and poorly explored avenue for addressing this problem is asteroseismology, which provides the most stringent constraints on internal structure and evolution. We investigated five SX Phoenicis stars from the core of the globular cluster ω Centauri that pulsate in two radial modes and occupy the blue-straggler region of the colour–magnitude diagram. Our seismic models were constructed assuming a collisional origin and compared with our previous seismic studies based on single-star evolution. For comparison, we also explored a binary evolution scenario involving mass transfer for one of the stars. The evolution of the parent stars was computed with MESA. The collision was then modelled with the MMAMS code, which reconstructs the merger remnant using an entropic variable. The subsequent evolution was followed up on with MESA up to the current age of the cluster. Finally, we constructed seismic models that reproduce the observed frequencies of the two radial modes. We present the first seismic modelling of SX Phe (blue straggler) stars based on the collision-formation scenario. Convective-core overshooting is essential for rejuvenation and for obtaining seismic models in the main sequence phase of evolution, but it is not always sufficient. Whether a merger remnant undergoes rejuvenation depends in a complex way on the masses of the parent stars, metallicity, and collision time. We identified three evolutionary behaviours: no, delayed, and immediate rejuvenation. The collisional seismic models imply younger ages and higher masses than the seismic models based on single-star evolution.

title: Kesadaran Mahasiswa terhadap Pentingnya Tidur yang Cukup pada Masa Aktivitas Akademik yang Padat: Studi Kualitatif pada Mahasiswa Universitas Riau
abstractText: Aktivitas akademik yang padat pada jenjang pendidikan tinggi sering kali memaksa mahasiswa mengorbankan waktu istirahat, sehingga memicu penurunan kualitas hidup dan konsentrasi belajar. Penelitian kualitatif ini bertujuan untuk mendeskripsikan secara mendalam tingkat kesadaran mahasiswa terhadap pentingnya tidur yang cukup, menganalisis pola adaptasi tidur mereka, serta mengidentifikasi faktor-faktor yang melatarbelakangi hambatan tersebut. Metode penelitian yang digunakan adalah deskriptif kualitatif dengan teknik pengumpulan data berupa wawancara mendalam terhadap mahasiswa aktif Universitas Riau dari berbagai fakultas yang dipilih secara purposive. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa meskipun mahasiswa memiliki kesadaran kognitif yang baik mengenai urgensi tidur, mereka mengalami dilema struktural akibat beban penugasan yang menumpuk. Pola tidur mahasiswa terganggu secara kronis akibat adanya budaya prokrastinasi akademik dan tingginya kecemasan menjelang tenggat waktu tugas. Penelitian ini menyimpulkan bahwa terdapat benturan nyata antara kebutuhan biologis tubuh dengan tuntutan performa akademik mahasiswa di lingkungan universitas.

title: Strategi Komunikasi Coffee Shop Goodhands dalam Menarik Minat Konsumen
abstractText: Persaingan usaha Coffee Shop menuntut pelaku usaha menerapkan strategi komunikasi pemasaran yang efektif untuk menarik perhatian dan meningkatkan minat kunjungan konsumen. Penelitian ini bertujuan menganalisis strategi komunikasi Coffee Shop Goodhands dalam menarik minat konsumen berdasarkan model AISAS (Attention, Interest, Search, Action, dan Share). Penelitian menggunakan pendekatan kualitatif dengan jenis deskriptif. Informan berjumlah enam orang yang terdiri atas satu pemilik usaha, dua karyawan, dan tiga konsumen yang dipilih melalui teknik purposive sampling. Data dikumpulkan melalui observasi nonpartisipan, wawancara semi-terstruktur, dan dokumentasi, kemudian dianalisis menggunakan model Miles dan Huberman. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa tahap Attention dibangun melalui konten visual Instagram yang menampilkan produk, suasana, dan kegiatan Goodhands. Tahap Interest didukung oleh kualitas produk, konsep interior bergaya vintage, pelayanan, dan kegiatan live music. Pada tahap Search, Instagram menjadi sumber informasi mengenai menu, harga, lokasi, dan kegiatan. Tahap Action dipengaruhi oleh promosi, rekomendasi teman, serta pengalaman konsumen, sedangkan tahap Share terlihat melalui unggahan dan rekomendasi langsung. Namun, tahap Action dan Share belum berjalan optimal. Penelitian ini menyimpulkan bahwa Goodhands perlu memperkuat konsistensi konten, promosi kegiatan, dan keterlibatan konsumen untuk meningkatkan efektivitas komunikasi serta minat kunjungan.

title: Pergeseran Penggunaan Bahasa Indonesia Akibat Tren Bahasa Gaul di Kalangan Generasi Muda
abstractText: Bahasa santai yang banyak digunakan di media digital dan lingkungan pergaulan mahasiswa vokasi membuat sulit bagi mereka untuk menguasai bahasa Indonesia yang baku, yang diperlukan ketika mereka akan memasuki dunia kerja profesional. Penelitian ini mencoba memahami apa saja yang menyebabkan orang menggunakan bahasa gaul, bagaimana penggunaan bahasa gaul memengaruhi kemampuan berbicara dalam bahasa Indonesia yang benar, dan bagaimana cara meningkatkan kesadaran untuk menggunakan bahasa baku tanpa menghilangkan penggunaan bahasa gaul dalam kehidupan sehari-hari. Penelitian ini menggunakan pendekatan campuran melalui survei online dengan kuesioner kepada 33 mahasiswa, sebagian besar berasal dari Fakultas Vokasi Universitas Brawijaya angkatan 2026 (sekitar 84,8%) serta wawancara mendalam dengan dua narasumber. Hasil penelitian dianalisis secara deskriptif dan tematik menggunakan metode statistik. Penelitian menunjukkan bahwa sekitar 87,9% orang menggunakan bahasa gaul. Hal ini disebabkan oleh pengaruh media sosial sebesar 51,5%, interaksi dengan teman sebaya sebesar 36,4%, serta keinginan untuk merasa dekat dengan orang lain sebesar 69,7%. Dampak terhadap kemampuan bahasa berlangsung tidak merata: mahasiswa dapat mempertahankan keakuratan bahasa dalam tugas tulis (81,8%), tetapi mengalami penurunan jumlah kata baku yang digunakan (60,6%) serta kesulitan dalam pemilihan kata saat presentasi lisan (45,4%). Semua responden (100%) setuju untuk menerapkan alih kode situasional. Dalam simulasi komunikasi profesional, sebanyak 51,5% dianggap paling efektif dibandingkan dengan larangan normatif.

title: Kepercayaan Diri Sebagai Faktor Pendukung Keterampilan Komunikasi dalam Bahasa Arab
abstractText: Kepercayaan diri merupakan salah satu aspek penting dalam pembelajaran bahasa Arab, khususnya pada keterampilan berbicara (maharah al-kalam), karena keterampilan ini menuntut keberanian untuk menggunakan bahasa secara lisan. Banyak pembelajar sudah memahami kosakata dan kaidah tata bahasa, tetapi belum mampu menggunakannya dalam percakapan karena merasa tidak yakin, takut salah, atau khawatir mendapat respons buruk dari orang lain. Artikel ini bertujuan menjelaskan peran kepercayaan diri dalam mendukung keterampilan berkomunikasi bahasa Arab, faktor-faktor yang memengaruhinya, serta upaya untuk meningkatkannya. Penelitian ini menggunakan pendekatan kualitatif deskriptif dengan metode penelitian kepustakaan (library research), yaitu menelaah buku, jurnal ilmiah, dan sumber tertulis lain yang relevan. Hasil kajian menunjukkan bahwa kepercayaan diri meningkatkan keberanian berbicara, membantu pembelajar memandang kesalahan sebagai bagian dari proses belajar, dan mendorong konsistensi berlatih. Namun, kepercayaan diri bukan satu-satunya penentu keberhasilan, karena penguasaan kosakata, semangat belajar, latihan, dan suasana belajar juga berpengaruh. Kepercayaan diri dipengaruhi oleh penguasaan kosakata dan kaidah tata bahasa, pengalaman belajar, lingkungan pembelajaran, dan rasa takut melakukan kesalahan. Upaya untuk meningkatkannya antara lain membiasakan percakapan sederhana, berlatih secara berpasangan, dan menciptakan lingkungan belajar yang mendukung.

title: Analisis Pendekatan Personal Selling Beauty Advisor Berbasis Skin Analysis terhadap Keputusan Pembelian Konsumen pada Toko Ettra Kosmetik
abstractText: Persaingan industri kosmetik dan skincare mendorong toko ritel menghadirkan layanan yang lebih personal bagi konsumen. Penelitian ini bertujuan mendeskripsikan dan menganalisis pendekatan personal selling Beauty Advisor berbasis skin analysis serta kaitannya dengan keputusan pembelian konsumen pada Toko Ettra Kosmetik. Penelitian menggunakan pendekatan kualitatif deskriptif. Data dikumpulkan melalui observasi non-partisipatif, wawancara semi-terstruktur, dan dokumentasi selama Praktik Kerja Lapangan pada 31 Agustus sampai 20 November 2026, kemudian dianalisis melalui reduksi data, penyajian data, dan penarikan kesimpulan. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa personal selling dijalankan secara konsultatif, adaptif, dan berorientasi pada hubungan, mulai dari approach, identifikasi kebutuhan, presentasi produk dengan tester, penanganan keberatan, closing yang tidak agresif, hingga follow-up. Skin analysis memperkuat tahap identifikasi kebutuhan sehingga rekomendasi produk disesuaikan dengan kondisi kulit, usia, kebiasaan perawatan, dan anggaran konsumen. Kendala utama meliputi ketidaksediaan sebagian konsumen menjalani skin analysis, toko yang ramai, dan ketidaktersediaan stok produk yang direkomendasikan. Penelitian ini belum membuktikan hubungan sebab-akibat antara skin analysis dan keputusan pembelian.

title: Loyalitas Pemandu Wisata Citumang: Ditinjau dari Perspektif Gig Economy dan Kesejahteraan
abstractText: Pemandu wisata merupakan tenaga kerja tidak tetap yang menopang operasional destinasi wisata alam, tetapi sistem kerjanya yang berbasis permintaan menghadirkan fleksibilitas sekaligus ketidakpastian yang berpotensi memengaruhi loyalitas. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk mendeskripsikan gig economy, kesejahteraan, dan loyalitas, serta menganalisis pengaruh gig economy dan kesejahteraan, baik secara simultan maupun parsial, terhadap loyalitas pemandu wisata di Wisata Alam Citumang, Kabupaten Pangandaran. Penelitian menggunakan metode kuantitatif dengan pendekatan deskriptif dan verifikatif. Populasi penelitian adalah seluruh pemandu wisata yang aktif bekerja, yaitu 30 orang, dengan teknik sampling jenuh (sensus). Data dikumpulkan melalui kuesioner berskala Likert dan dianalisis menggunakan regresi linier berganda dengan bantuan IBM SPSS Statistics 26. Seluruh item instrumen dinyatakan valid dan reliabel (Cronbach's Alpha sebesar 0,837 untuk gig economy, 0,883 untuk kesejahteraan, dan 0,925 untuk loyalitas). Hasil analisis deskriptif menunjukkan bahwa gig economy (rata-rata 4,38), kesejahteraan (4,36), dan loyalitas (4,56) berada pada kategori sangat tinggi. Hasil uji hipotesis menunjukkan bahwa gig economy dan kesejahteraan secara simultan berpengaruh signifikan terhadap loyalitas (F = 22,396; sig. 0,000), dan secara parsial masing-masing berpengaruh positif dan signifikan, dengan gig economy memberikan pengaruh yang relatif lebih dominan (Beta 0,527 dibandingkan 0,345). Kedua variabel secara bersama-sama menjelaskan 62,4% variasi loyalitas (R² = 0,624). Penelitian ini menyimpulkan bahwa fleksibilitas kerja dan kesejahteraan yang dirasakan pemandu berkontribusi nyata terhadap loyalitas, sehingga pengelola destinasi perlu memperkuat perlindungan sosial dan kepastian pendapatan bagi pemandu wisata.

title: Pemberdayaan Masyarakat Berbasis Eco-Masjid Melalui Program Sedekah Sampah di Desa Wangandowo
abstractText: Salah satu kunci menciptakan kemandirian komunitas di desa yaitu dengan mengembangkan potensi Masyarakat dengan cara mengoptimalisasikan asset lokal serta adanya dukungan serta peran dari Masyarakat sekitar. Di Desa Wangandowo, Kabupaten pekalongan, pengelolaan sampah anorganik masih terfokus pada penangan masalah secara konvensional yang belum menggali dari segi nilai ekonomis serta modal sosial warga di sekitar Masjid Baitul Mukmin. Kegiatan pengabdian ini bertujuan untuk mengembangkan potensi Masyarakat melalui program Eco-Masjid berbasis sedekah sampah untuk mendukung operasional masjid serta menumbuhkan kesadaran ekologis masyarakat sekitar. Penelitian ini menggunakan metode Asset-Based Community Development (ABCD) melalui lima tahapan Appreciative Inquiry (Discovery, Dream, Design, Define, Destiny) dengan dukungan takmir, Jemaah masjid, pemuda pemudi sebagai penggerak utama program serta mahasiswa KKN sebagai fasilitator. Hasil pemetaan berhasil mengidentifikasi dan memobilisasi enam dimensi aset komunitas yang meliputi modal manusia, sosial, kelembagaan, fisik/alam, finansial, dan spiritual-budaya. Secara operasional, potensi tersebut diwujudkan melalui adanya fasilitas dropbox, alat press botol manual, kemitraan dengan pengepul desa, serta pengelolaan pencatatan keuangan digital melalui Aplikasi Sedekah Sampah. Aksi penimbangan tahap awal mengonversi 42 kg sampah anorganik yang terdiri dari 40 kg botol plastik dan 2 kg kardus bekas, hasil tersebut menjadi dana kas infak masjid sebesar Rp68.000,00 secara transparan. Pembingkaian nilai keagamaan (thaharah dan amal jariyah) optimalisasi keterlibatan Masyarakat melalui penguatan pilar kemandirian terbukti mampu mengubah potensi sampah snorganik menjadi wujud kebersamaan dan solidaritas yang kolektif. Disimpulkan bahwa strategi pengembangan potensi berbasis kekuatan internal efektif meningkatkan partisipasi aktif warga, kemandirian ekonomi kelembagaan masjid, dan keberlanjutan pelestarian lingkungan.

title: Pemanfaatan ChatGPT sebagai Media Komunikasi dan Literasi pada Mahasiswa Universitas Malikussaleh
abstractText: Perkembangan teknologi kecerdasan buatan telah mengubah pola komunikasi dan literasi mahasiswa, khususnya dalam memenuhi kebutuhan informasi dan aktivitas akademik. Penelitian ini bertujuan menganalisis pemanfaatan ChatGPT sebagai media komunikasi dan literasi serta kecenderungan ketergantungan mahasiswa Universitas Malikussaleh terhadap teknologi tersebut. Penelitian menggunakan pendekatan kualitatif dengan jenis deskriptif. Informan berjumlah tujuh mahasiswa yang dipilih melalui teknik purposive sampling berdasarkan frekuensi, durasi, dan intensitas penggunaan ChatGPT. Data dikumpulkan melalui observasi, wawancara semi-terstruktur, dan dokumentasi, kemudian dianalisis melalui tahapan pengumpulan data, reduksi data, penyajian data, serta penarikan dan verifikasi kesimpulan. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa mahasiswa memanfaatkan ChatGPT untuk mencari informasi, memahami materi perkuliahan, merangkum jurnal, menyusun tugas, dan mengembangkan gagasan akademik. Ketergantungan terhadap ChatGPT terlihat melalui efek kognitif berupa peningkatan kemudahan memahami materi, efek afektif berupa kenyamanan dan kepercayaan diri, serta efek perilaku berupa terbentuknya kebiasaan menggunakan ChatGPT sebagai pilihan awal dalam mencari informasi. Meskipun memberikan kemudahan, penggunaan berlebihan berpotensi mengurangi kemandirian berpikir mahasiswa. Penelitian ini menyimpulkan bahwa ChatGPT perlu dimanfaatkan secara bijaksana sebagai media pendukung komunikasi dan literasi dengan tetap mengutamakan verifikasi informasi, literasi kritis, dan kemandirian belajar.

title: miRNA Regulation of the FGF23-Klotho Pathway Mitigates Adverse Cardiac Remodeling During Nocturnal Hemodialysis
abstractText: Background: Cardiovascular disease (CVD) remains the leading cause of morbidity and mortality in patients with ESKD. Dysregulation of the fibroblast growth factor 23 (FGF23)/Klotho axis has been implicated in uremic cardiomyopathy, however the mechanism linking dialysis intensity to the regulation of this pathway remains poorly defined. Methods: We analyzed serum samples from ESKD patients transitioning from conventional to nocturnal hemodialysis (NHD). Left ventricular mass (LVM) was measured by echocardiography before and after transition. Patients were stratified as LVM regressors [ ≥ 10% decrease in LVM; n = 6] or LVM progressors [ ≥ 10% increase in LVM; n = 7]. Circulating microRNAs (miRs) and serum FGF23 and alpha Klotho were quantified. Mechanistic relevance was tested in an angiotensin-II model of cardiac hypertrophy using FGF23 suppression via an antisense oligonucleotide gapmer, or antagomirs targeting miR-200c-3p. Results: Among 13 patients transitioning to NHD, LVM regressors required fewer antihypertensive medications than at baseline (P<0.001) with improved metabolic parameters (urea 12.9 vs. 16.6 mmol/L, P<0.01) and higher hemoglobin (109 vs. 95 g/L, P<0.01). We identified six differentially expressed miRs (let-7a/g/i, miR-200c, miR-1 and miR-30c) that targeted the FGF23/Klotho signaling axis. LVM regressors also demonstrated significantly lower circulating FGF23 levels than LVM progressors [60 (28, 160) vs 668 (73, 1734) pg/mL, P<0.05]. In the angiotensin-II murine model of cardiac hypertrophy, FGF23 gapmer treatment or miR-200c-3p inhibition reduced cardiomyocyte hypertrophy and attenuated interstitial fibrosis while restoring FGF23/Klotho signaling through the suppression of extracellular signal-regulated kinase 1/2 phosphorylation, activation of dual specificity phosphatase-1 and inducing antioxidant gene expression. Conclusions: Collectively, these exploratory findings link dialysis intensification to miR-mediated regulation of the FGF23/Klotho axis, demonstrating that targeting this regulatory network is sufficient to suppress pathological cardiac remodeling. These data provide a mechanistic basis for the cardiovascular benefits of nocturnal hemodialysis and identify the FGF23/Klotho axis as a candidate therapeutic target warranting further validation.

title: Adolescent-responsive sexual and reproductive health services in Asia-Pacific settings: a systematic scoping review
abstractText: In the Asia-Pacific region, adolescents face significant impacts from unintended pregnancy and are disproportionately affected by the growing HIV epidemic. Despite decades of policy commitments, adolescents have high unmet need for sexual and reproductive health services. The World Health Organization’s 2015 global standards for quality adolescent health services provide a framework, but evidence of their implementation in the region remains limited. This systematic scoping review mapped approaches to adolescent-responsive sexual and reproductive health service delivery in Asia-Pacific low- and middle-income countries and factors influencing implementation. On 6 January 2026, three databases (Medline, Embase and Scopus) were searched for peer-reviewed literature published between January 2019 and December 2025. In line with scoping review methodology, methodological quality was not assessed. Twenty-five studies met the inclusion criteria, spanning nine South and Southeast Asian countries; none were from Pacific Island countries. The most evidence was available for Standards 1, 3 and 5. Where studies reported on equity and non-discrimination (Standard 6), and providers’ competencies (Standard 4), they described shortfalls, although evidence on competencies was mixed. Few studies reported on community support, data and quality improvement, or adolescents’ participation (Standards 2, 7 and 8), reflecting limited available evidence. These findings underscore priorities for investment in adolescent health. More comprehensive, adolescent-centred sexual and reproductive health services and action on stigma are needed, with adolescent engagement and co-leadership central to this shift. Self-care may complement formal health systems, although evidence of its effectiveness in the region remains limited.

Social media, brand image, and price perception as predictors of purchase decisions: Evidence from kopi kenangan consumers in Manado, Indonesia
abstractText: This study examines whether social media, brand image, and price perception are associated with the purchase decisions of Kopi Kenangan consumers in Manado, Indonesia, a regional market in which prior findings for this brand are mixed. A cross-sectional questionnaire survey of 100 customers, recruited through purposive sampling offline and online, was analyzed with multiple linear regression. Social media and brand image were positively and significantly associated with purchase decisions, with effects of comparable and moderate size. Price perception showed no significant association, and its confidence interval included zero, so no direction of effect can be inferred. Together, the three predictors explained about one quarter of the variance in purchase decisions. The study provides jointly estimated effects, confidence intervals, and effect sizes for three commonly studied predictors in an Eastern Indonesian city. Informative social media content and a consistent brand image are associated with purchase decisions, whereas the study offers no evidence for or against a price-perception association. Non-probability sampling, a single time point, self-reported data, and modestly reliable price and purchase-decision scales limit generalization.

title: Dry Surface Decontamination of Nerve (A-234, GF, GD) and Blister (HD) Chemical Warfare Agents Using TiO2/CeO2 Nanosorbents
abstractText: Abstract Dry surface decontamination is a highly practical approach for mitigating chemical warfare agent (CWA) threats without generating liquid waste. Herein, we systematically investigate the dry decontamination performance of nanoscale TiO2, CeO2, and mixed TiO2/CeO2 (TiCe) sorbents against nerve (A-234, GF, GD) and blister (HD) agents. Materials characterization confirms that mixing Ti and Ce shifts the microstructure into a highly open, mesoporous network, significantly expanding the total pore volume to 1.01 cm3/g. In dry batch experiments, all nanosorbents achieved rapid, complete depletion of parent extractable G-agents within 10 min, while the Novichok agent A-234 was reduced to <4% within 10 min, exhibiting comparable performance under both ambient daylight and complete darkness. To the best of our knowledge, this work represents the first demonstration of fully dry Novichok detoxification using metal oxide-based sorbents. Blister agent HD underwent slower degradation, achieving near-complete depletion (with <3% residual) after 480 min. GC–MS analysis confirmed that depletion is driven by safe hydrolytic pathways yielding low-toxicity derivatives, without hazardous oxidation byproducts. When applied to contaminated ceramic tiles, the dry powders successfully transferred and removed all parent CWAs to levels undetectable by GC–FID and GC–MS in both immediate and aged scenarios, except for A-234 on CeO2 (3.7% residue). These findings demonstrate that practical dry surface decontamination is governed by rapid mechanical transfer followed by intra-sorbent degradation. Furthermore, the successful up-scaling of the nanoporous TiO2 synthesis to a kilo-lab scale highlights the straightforward scalability of these materials for real-world applications on delicate equipment.

title: A Mixed Methods Study of Students' Catholic Educational Experience and School Leaders' Perspectives in a Non-Sectarian School
abstractText: This mixed methods study examined students’ Catholic educational experiences and school leaders’ perspectives on sustaining Catholic values within San Pablo Colleges, a non-sectarian institution in San Pablo City, Laguna. Specifically, it assessed students’ perceived level of Catholicity, the influence of institutional education on faith and moral development, and the leadership strategies and challenges associated with maintaining Catholic identity in an inclusive educational environment. The study employed a mixed methods research design involving 299 students selected through stratified random sampling and six school heads selected purposively. Quantitative data were gathered using a validated survey questionnaire and analyzed through descriptive statistics, while qualitative data were obtained through written interviews and examined using thematic analysis. Findings revealed a high perceived level of Catholicity (M = 3.18) and a high influence of institutional education on faith development (M = 3.08). Moral development received a very high rating (M = 3.33), emphasizing human dignity, service orientation, ethical decision-making, and values integration. Qualitative findings highlighted transformational leadership, teacher modeling, institutional culture, and service-learning as essential mechanisms for sustaining Catholic identity. However, students demonstrated comparatively moderate participation in structured religious activities, indicating a gap between internalized values and religious practices. Based on these findings, a Faith Engagement Innovation Plan was proposed to strengthen student-centered faith formation, liturgical participation, reflective service-learning, and digital faith initiatives. The study concluded that Catholic identity can be sustained within non-sectarian educational settings through inclusive leadership, moral formation, and meaningful faith engagement.

title: Comparison of the efficacy and safety of carbapenem versus other β-lactam antibiotics with anti-Pseudomonas aeruginosa activity in the initial treatment of febrile neutropenia: a target trial emulation using large-scale health insurance claims database in Japan
abstractText: Abstract Background Carbapenem resistance has recently become an issue, and carbapenem-sparing therapies have been adopted accordingly. For the initial treatment of febrile neutropenia (FN), carbapenems and other β-lactam antibiotics with anti- Pseudomonas aeruginosa ( P. aeruginosa ) activity are recommended. This study aimed to compare the efficacy and safety of initial treatment strategies using carbapenems versus cephalosporins with anti- P. aeruginosa activity (CEP) or piperacillin/tazobactam (PTZ) for FN. Methods Using the JMDC hospital-based database, we conducted a target trial comparing the strategy of initiating carbapenems with that of initiating CEP/PTZ for FN. Cancer patients who developed FN after initial chemotherapy and received targeted antibiotics between April 2014 and August 2025 were identified. Patients were classified into the carbapenem and CEP/PTZ groups based on the initial antibiotic selection. Stabilized inverse probability of treatment weighting based on propensity scores was used to adjust the balance of baseline patient characteristics. The primary endpoint was the 28-day mortality. Secondary endpoints included the antibiotic class-switching rate, treatment duration, addition of anti-methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (anti-MRSA) agents, addition of antifungal agents, incidence of Clostridioides difficile infection (CDI), and therapeutic use of granulocyte colony-stimulating factor (G-CSF). Results Among 4468 patients in the study (CEP/PTZ group, 3791; carbapenem group, 677), no significant difference in 28-day mortality was observed between the groups (HR, 1.164; 95% CI, 0.783–1.732; p = 0.453). Antibiotic class switching was significantly more frequent in the CEP/PTZ group than in the carbapenem group (23.6% vs. 12.4%; sHR, 0.411; 95% CI, 0.320–0.527; p < 0.001), whereas the addition of anti-MRSA agents was more frequent in the carbapenem group than in the CEP/PTZ group (15.9% vs. 11.5%; sHR, 1.544; 95% CI, 1.173–2.031; p = 0.002). No significant differences were observed in the treatment duration, addition of antifungal agents, incidence of CDI, or therapeutic use of G-CSF. Conclusions No significant difference in 28-day mortality was observed between the strategy of initiating carbapenems and that of initiating CEP/PTZ, although antibiotic class switching was more frequent in the latter. From the perspective of carbapenem-sparing, initiating CEP/PTZ with escalation when clinically indicated may be a reasonable option for the initial treatment of FN.

title: Hubungan Brand Differentiation Dengan Loyalitas Konsumen: Studi Kasus Pada Kahyangan Jewelry
abstractText: Penelitian ini bertujuan menganalisis hubungan diferensiasi merek (brand differentiation) dengan loyalitas konsumen Kahyangan Jewelry dalam perspektif Customer-Based Brand Equity (CBBE), dengan autentisitas merek sebagai mediator dan kepercayaan merek sebagai moderator. Survei potong lintang eksplanatori ini melibatkan 161 konsumen perempuan yang telah membeli minimal dua kali dan dipilih secara purposive, sehingga temuan terbatas pada konsumen yang sudah loyal. Data dianalisis menggunakan PROCESS Macro Hayes Model 14 dengan 5.000 resampel bootstrap. Diferensiasi merek berhubungan positif dengan autentisitas merek (b = 0.53) dan loyalitas konsumen (b = 0.53). Autentisitas merek tidak terbukti memediasi hubungan tersebut, sedangkan interaksi autentisitas merek dan kepercayaan merek bernilai negatif (b = −0.24; p = .025). Indeks moderated mediation signifikan (−0.13), tetapi seluruh efek tidak langsung bersyarat tidak signifikan. Efek langit-langit (ceiling effect) pada data membatasi generalisasi dan interpretasi koefisien.

title: Essential medicine policies in a transitioning health system: a systematic review from Lao PDR
abstractText: Abstract Background Access to medicines is central to achieving Universal Health Coverage. Lao PDR has implemented essential medicines policies for more than two decades; however, significant access challenges persist, particularly in the context of limited fiscal space and health system transition. The objective of this review was to describe medicine systems and policies of Laos, a small and low-resource country, to identify areas that could be strengthened to improve access to essential medicines. Methods A systematic literature review was conducted to describe the organisation, policies and functions of the medication systems in Lao PDR and the influence they have on access to essential medicines. Scientific and grey literature published in English and Lao language up to March 2026 were reviewed. Data were analysed thematically across five core medication system constituents. Policy documents were analysed to understand the context, contents, processes and influencing actors. Consistency between documented policies and reported practices was assessed through interviews with relevant stakeholders. Findings A total of 241 documents were included. Lao PDR has established policies and legislations for a functional medicine system, though its journey towards Universal Health Coverage is hindered by an implementation gap. The National Health Insurance scheme has improved access and reduced out-of-pocket spending, achieving its target of keeping it below 35% of total health spending. However, systemic weaknesses create persistent barriers to medicine access. These include inadequate financing, weak enforcement of legislations, misaligned policies and inefficient procurement. Conclusion The findings provide a roadmap for policy reform to enhance evidence use, financing, and governance, which is essential for Lao PDR and other low-income settings navigating health system transitions.

title: Tinjauan Kritis Model Lima Kekuatan Porter untuk Teknologi Additive Manufacturing: Perspektif Ekonomi Industri dan Metodologi Penelitian
abstractText: This study presents a critical review of the article by Soraya Dias, Pedro Espadinha-Cruz, and Florinda Matos (2023) entitled "A Porter’s Five Forces Model Proposal for Additive Manufacturing Technology: A Case Study in Portuguese industry" in Procedia Computer Science (Vol. 217, pp. 165–176). Evaluated through research methodology and industrial organization economics, this review examines the validity and economic logic of adapting Porter’s Five Forces to Additive Manufacturing (AM) across 13 Portuguese firms. Methodologically, the study exhibits a mismatch between its claimed qualitative exploratory case study design and its execution as a descriptive web survey without thematic coding or inferential testing. Severe selection bias arises because 12 of 13 firms use AM only as an auxiliary prototyping tool (61% report zero final-product weight), alongside contradictions between tables and text (notably the 92% AM knowledge access figure in Table 5 and cross-table misreferencing). Economically, the authors conflate a production process technology with a distinct market boundary, overlooking marginal cost trade-offs between economies of scale and scope, oligopolistic supplier concentration versus low switching costs, labor market friction, and public-good externalities in unprotected intellectual property rights (IPR).

title: Open-access tools to characterize potential DART, DNT, and endocrine-related effects from cannabis and contaminants: addressing concerns for health disparities and exposure during pregnancy
abstractText: Expanding cannabis legislation may increase access to and use of Cannabis sativa products containing delta-9-tetrahydrocannabinol ( Δ9- THC) and cannabidiol (CBD) among pregnant and breastfeeding individuals, raising concerns about developmental and reproductive toxicity (DART), developmental neurotoxicity (DNT), and endocrine disruption. Populations with limited access to prenatal care, reliable health information, or regulated cannabis products may experience greater exposure uncertainty. We evaluated new approach methodologies (NAMs) to investigate potential developmental and pregnancy-related hazards associated with Δ9- THC, CBD, and selected pesticide contaminants used in cannabis production. NAMs, including the Generalized Read-Across (GenRA) tool, the Toxicity Estimation Software Tool (TEST), Cheminformatics, Predicting Developmental Toxicity Potential Project (PredPreg), and OrbiTox, were used to predict DART, DNT, and endocrine disruption potential for Δ9- THC, CBD, and the pesticide contaminants chlorfenapyr (CFP), trifloxystrobin (TRI), and piperonyl butoxide (PBO). ToxCast data were used as inputs for Integrated Chemical Environment adult and maternal/fetal physiologically based toxicokinetic (PBTK) models to generate adjusted administered equivalent dose (AdjAED) estimates, which were compared with available in vivo points of departure. Each NAM identified potential DART- and DNT-related hazards for the five chemicals. ToxCast results supported the biological plausibility of developmental and endocrine effects across all chemicals. Adult and fetal PBTK-predicted AdjAEDs generally agreed within an order of magnitude with measured in vivo points of departure. Overall findings demonstrate that open-access NAMs can identify potential developmental hazards associated with Δ9- THC, CBD, and pesticide contaminants while addressing data gaps, prioritize chemicals for further investigation, and inform future studies. Results highlight the importance of reducing exposure uncertainty and improving prenatal risk communication.

Short-term results of arthroscopic partial trapeziectomy with hematoma distraction for basal thumb osteoarthritis
abstractText: Background: Arthroscopic partial trapeziectomy combined with different interpositions and ligament reconstruction procedures is gaining popularity now as a viable alternative to traditional surgery. This study was designed to evaluate the clinical and radiological outcomes of arthroscopic partial trapeziectomy with hematoma distraction of the trapeziometacarpal joint in basal thumb osteoarthritis. Methods: In this prospective case series, 35 patients with stages II and III trapeziometacarpal osteoarthritis were treated with arthroscopic partial trapeziectomy and hematoma distraction by K-wires and followed up for 24 mo. Outcome measures included the Disabilities of the Arm, Shoulder, and Hand (DASH) questionnaire, the visual analogue scale for pain, grip strength, and pinch strength. Results: After 24 months, DASH improved from a mean of 55.4 ± 12.6 to a mean of 13 ± 5.3, visual analogue scale improved from a mean of 5.4 ± 1.9 to a mean of 1.4 ± 1.3, grip strength improved from a mean of 21.4 ± 12.1 kg to a mean of 26 ± 10.5 kg, and pinch strength improved from a mean of 4.1 ± 2.1 kg to a mean of 4.9 ± 2.5 kg. Conclusions: Arthroscopic partial trapeziectomy with hematoma distraction procedure yielded favorable outcomes and can be an effective choice for stage II and III basal thumb osteoarthritis with notable pain relief and good thumb motion. Surgical versus non-surgical treatment for metacarpal shaft fractures: a prospective feasibility study
abstractText: Aims The aims of this study were to assess the feasibility of a randomized controlled trial (RCT) comparing surgical and non-surgical treatment for metacarpal shaft fractures (MSFs), identify appropriate outcome measures for use in a future trial, and provide person-centred insight to inform trial design and identify barriers to participation. Methods We carried out a prospective, multicentre, observational feasibility study at five UK sites, and an embedded qualitative study. Adults (aged ≥ 16 years) with an acute displaced MSF were screened and prospectively recruited between July 2020 and July 2021. Clinical (grip strength, range of motion, and radiological parameters) and patient-reported outcome measures (Patient Evaluation Measure, the abbreviated version of the Disabilities of the Arm, Shoulder and Hand questionnaire (QuickDASH), Patient-Reported Outcomes Measurement Information System Upper Extremity (PROMIS-UE), EQ-5D-5L, and the seven-point Global Rating of Change) were collected at study enrollment, six weeks, and at three, and six months. Semistructured interviews and focus groups were conducted with participants selected from the main study cohort using purposive sampling, and analyzed using a thematic inductive approach. Results Of 5,863 patients screened, 201 were eligible and 108 were recruited. The median age was 32 years (IQR 22 to 48); 68% (n = 73/108) patients were male, 84% (n = 65/108) were treated non-surgically, and 16% (n = 12/108) surgically. Treatment was unknown for 31 patients (29%) who failed to attend the six-week follow-up. Retention was 71% (n = 77/108) at six weeks and 45% (n = 49/108) at six months. In total, 20 interviews were conducted, with 13 participants and three focus groups (eight participants per group). Five key themes and 30 sub-themes were identified. Participants selected the QuickDASH and PROMIS-UE as optimal outcome measures and recommended increased follow-up in the first four to six weeks post-injury. Interventions, data collection methods, and follow-up were acceptable to participants. Conclusion A multicentre RCT comparing surgical and non-surgical management of MSF appears feasible. Recruitment across sites was achievable and suitable primary outcome measures were identified. However, declining retention beyond six weeks highlights the need for targeted strategies to enhance engagement and retention in a definitive trial. title: Integrated CO2-EOR and Post-EOR Storage in a Mature Waterflooded UKCS Sandstone Reservoir: Recovery-Retention-Pressure Trade-offs from Compositional Simulation
abstractText: Abstract This study evaluates miscible CO2-enhanced oil recovery, post-EOR CO2 storage, and long-term postinjection behavior in a mature offshore sandstone reservoir using compositional simulation. A PVT-tuned Peng–Robinson model gave a pure-CO2 minimum miscibility pressure of 2,528 psia by the multiple-mixing-cell method, and reservoir pressure remained above this value in all CO2-EOR cases. Five strategies (continuous CO2; fixed and tapered water-alternating-gas (WAG); a CO2 slug followed by WAG; and simultaneous water-and-gas injection) were compared from a common 2027 reference state. A 36-month CO2 slug followed by alternating six-month CO2 and six-month water periods was preferred: it produced 69.61 MMstb (8.64% of stock-tank oil initially in place), 50.06 MMstb more than continued waterflooding, and retained 9.86 of 21.42 Mt injected CO2 (46.0%). Post-EOR storage at 140 MMscf/d for 15 years, selected from three rate cases because injectivity rather than nominal rate controlled the stored mass, raised the total retained CO2 to 44.81 Mt (79.5% of 56.37 Mt injected); field-average pressure then declined from 6,955 to 6,385 psia over 100 years of shut-in monitoring. Plume expansion was limited, CO2 partitioned progressively into the oleic and aqueous phases, and mobile gas-phase CO2 decreased. The results show that a single mature, heavily waterflooded UKCS reservoir can deliver 6.2 percentage points of additional recovery and retain close to 45 Mt CO2 within its estimated operating-pressure envelope, providing a quantified reservoir-engineering basis for repurposing late-life North Sea oil fields as CO2 storage sites. Geomechanical, well-integrity, surface-processing, economic and lifecycle assessments are required before implementation.

title: TDECat : A comparative study of tidal disruption event host galaxies
abstractText: Tidal disruption events (TDEs) occur when a star is disrupted by the tidal field of a supermassive black hole, which produces a luminous transient flare. The properties of TDE host galaxies provide an observational route for studying the nuclear environments in which these events occur, but previous structural studies have often been limited by smaller samples or heterogeneous imaging. We present the largest systematic photometric and structural analysis of confirmed TDE host galaxies to date from using Pan-STARRS g- and r-band imaging. modelling yields reliable surface-brightness decompositions for 109 hosts in the r band and 100 hosts in the g band, making this the largest homogeneous structural sample of TDE hosts to date. The approximate rest-frame (g-r) colour analysis yields a Monte Carlo green-valley count of TDECat GALFIT ̊m GV =20^ +3 _ -2 out of the 95 colour-classified hosts, corresponding to approximately 21%, compared with the ∼47–63% fractions reported in previous studies. Structurally, the hosts are generally compact and moderately concentrated, with a median effective radius of R_ e =1.64 kpc and a median Sérsic index of n=3.24. Comparisons of multi-wavelength and optical spectral subsamples show only limited structural separations, suggesting that global host-galaxy structure alone does not determine the observed diversity of TDE properties. Overall, the results indicate that TDE hosts share recurring photometric and structural tendencies but form a broader and more diverse population than implied by a single preferred host class.
