Perspectives on Language-Concordant Medical Device Education for Children With Medical Complexity
abstractText: BACKGROUND/OBJECTIVE Children with medical complexity (CMC) with caregivers who use a language other than English (LOE) are at higher risk of medical device complications after hospitalization and may not receive discharge medical device education in their preferred language. We sought to explore key implementation facilitators and barriers to providing language-concordant discharge medical device education from the perspectives of case managers and medical device vendors. METHODS We conducted semistructured interviews, informed by existing literature and the Consolidated Framework for Implementation Research (CFIR) conceptual model, with a national, geographically diverse sample of pediatric hospital case managers and medical device vendors. We audio-recorded and transcribed interviews and continued data collection until we reached thematic sufficiency. We conducted a thematic analysis using inductive coding to identify salient themes and then mapped themes to the CFIR. RESULTS We conducted 24 interviews (13 case managers and 11 vendors). Facilitators included vendors offering in-person teaching to optimize family-centered education and case managers supporting vendor use of hospital interpreters. Barriers included limited resources for vendors to provide interpreters or in-person education with skilled clinicians secondary to market pressures and individuals using suboptimal workarounds when interpreter access is limited. Participants proposed strategies including clear policies on vendor requirements for the provision of in-person, language-concordant education and opportunities to strengthen shared accountability between the hospital and vendors. CONCLUSIONS This study identified facilitators, barriers, and strategies to improve implementation of language-concordant medical device education for CMC-LOE families that can inform system- and policy-level changes to mitigate inequities and improve patient outcomes.

title: CH radical addition to pentatetraenylidene: An efficient gas-phase route to C_6H_2 in TMC-1
abstractText: The recent detection of several C_6H_2 isomers toward the cold Taurus molecular cloud TMC-1 has highlighted significant gaps in our understanding of the formation mechanisms of long carbon-chain species in the interstellar medium. Although previous theoretical and observational studies have proposed a variety of neutral-neutral and ion-neutral formation routes, astrochemical models still struggle to reproduce the observed abundances. We investigate the gas-phase reaction between the methylidyne radical (CH, X2Π$) and pentatetraenylidene (l-H_2C_5, X^1A$_1), both detected in TMC-1. High-level quantum-chemical calculations and master-equation kinetic simulations were used to characterize the reaction mechanism, rate coefficients, and product branching ratios. The reaction proceeds through a barrierless addition mechanism forming a strongly bound intermediate located 659 kJ mol -1 $ below the reactants. The computed global rate coefficients are about 10^-10 cm^3 molecule^-1 s^-1 over 30--300 K and display a weak non-monotonic temperature dependence. Master-equation calculations predict that triacetylene (HC_6H) accounts for approximately 99% of the total reactive flux. We also identify ethynylcyclobutatrienylidene (c-C_3HC_3H) as a previously unexplored cyclic member of the C_6H$_2 family and provide spectroscopic parameters for astronomical searches. The CH + l-H_2C_5 reaction is therefore a viable and rapid low-temperature pathway to triacetylene under conditions relevant to cold carbon-rich clouds. Incorporation of the calculated rate coefficients and branching ratios into astrochemical networks will allow us to assess its contribution to C_6H_2 chemistry in TMC-1 quantitatively.

title: Two new species of the family Linhomoeidae (Nematoda, Chromadorea, Monhysterida) from the South China Sea
abstractText: Two new species of free-living marine nematodes from the South China Sea, Desmolaimus sinicus sp. nov. and Eleutherolaimus longiseta sp. nov., are described and illustrated. Desmolaimus sinicus sp. nov. is characterized by its relatively small body compared to other species in the genus (except for Desmolaimus minor Gagarin, 2019, 440–588 µm in body length), cuticle smooth, four cephalic setae short, 2.5–3.5 µm long, amphidial fovea circular, located immediately posterior to the buccal cavity, buccal cavity conical flask-shaped, with a transverse cuticular ring in the middle, pharynx with well-developed posterior bulb, spicules arcuate, gubernaculum with dorso-caudal apophyses, tail conico-cylindrical with three short terminal setae. Eleutherolaimus longiseta sp. nov. is characterized by long cephalic setae, 12–15 µm in length, one medioventral setae and one mediodorsal setae (13–17 µm long) situated at level of buccal cavity base, one mediolateral setae situated immediately posterior to each amphid, circular amphidial fovea located at the level of the buccal cavity base, excretory pore situated posterior to the nerve ring, arcuate spicules 1.3–1.7 cloacal body diameters long, robust with capitulum projected dorsally, gubernaculum with straight sclerotized apophyses, tail conical, elongate in males with a pair of long dorsal subterminal setae and two longitudinal rows of subventral setae, female tail relatively shorter and without caudal setae. Identification keys to valid species of Desmolaimus and Eleutherolaimus are provided.

abstractText: Abstract With outstanding conductivity, tunable structure, and rich surface functional groups, two-dimensional (2D) MXene is extensively used for the electromagnetic interference (EMI) shielding field. However, MXene suffers from self-stacking and secondary reflection pollution, which weakens the electromagnetic wave (EMW) attenuation performance. Herein, we introduced one-dimensional (1D) PPy nanotubes (NTs) and (FeO)0.198(MnO)0.802 (FMO) magnetic nanoparticles derived from FeMn-metal–organic frameworks into the MXene system. Furthermore, combined with K+-induced filtration and freeze-drying technology, MXene/PPy NTs/FMO (MPFMO) composite films with three-dimensional (3D) porous structures were successfully constructed, thereby achieving significantly enhanced EMI shielding performances. The introduction of conductive PPy NTs not only refines the 3D conductive architecture embedded within the composite film but also induces forming hydrogen bonding and supports adjacent MXene nanosheets to increase the mechanical properties. The abundant heterogeneous interfaces can generate interfacial polarization and promote EMW absorption, and the intrinsic magnetic loss of FMO can further attenuate EMWs. Profiting from multiple synergy mechanisms, the MPFMO porous composite film delivers a high EMI SE of 62.43 dB, an absorption loss ratio of 72.50%, and specific shielding effectiveness SSEt of 1.21 × 104 dB cm2 g–1 at a thickness of only 55 μm. Notably, the as-prepared composite membrane also demonstrates a superior thermal conductivity of 18.82 W m–1 K–1.

Assessment of Biomass, Maximum Sustainable Yield, Size Distribution and Biodiversity of Demersal Large-scale Fisheries in Lake Malawi
abstractText: This study was conducted to assess the fish biomass, biodiversity patterns and sustainable harvesting potential of demersal large-scale fisheries in Lake Malawi. This study aimed to determine appropriate fisheries output management target points (total allowable catch (TAC) and maximum sustainable yield (MSY)). The assessment was conducted in 2024 and was based on fish biomass survey data from 2020, which was conducted on Lake Malawi by the Department of Fisheries. A stern trawler (RV Ndunduma) was fitted with a bottom trawl net with a code-end mesh size of 38 mm. Biomass was estimated using the swept-area method and MSY was estimated using the Beddington and Cooke model. Shannon, Simpson and Pielou’s evenness indices were employed to assess biodiversity, while non-parametric statistical tests such as PERMANOVA and Kruskal-Wallis were used to determine differences in fish community composition and fish size distributions across the regions of the lake. The study estimated the total fish biomass and MSY of demersal fisheries in Lake Malawi at 261,297.8 tons and 130,648.9 tons per year, respectively. The southern region of the lake contributed the highest proportion of biomass and MSY, accounting for 55.6% of the total biomass. The study recorded high fish species richness (152), predominantly demersal fish species and very low densities of midwater fish species. The southern part of the lake recorded the highest fish species richness and abundance; however, it also showed a significant regional difference in community composition and fish size distribution. The findings further showed that the following commercially important fish species, Diplotaxodon, Lethrinops, and Rhamphochromis, in the southern part of the lake had smaller mean body sizes than in other regions, suggesting possible excessive fishing effort and growth overexploitation. The study also revealed limitations in the current fish biomass assessment approach, which is biased toward demersal species and may underestimate midwater fish stocks targeted by large-scale fishers. This study demonstrates that sustainable fishery management in Lake Malawi requires region-specific allocation of fishers, improved fish biomass assessment, stricter enforcement of fishery regulations and enhanced conservation measures. This will ensure that fish biodiversity is protected and that there is long-term fishery productivity. The findings provide scientific information for guiding fisheries policy, TAC allocation and ecosystem-based fisheries management in Malawi. Key words: Trawl fishery, fish biomass assessment, demersal fisheries and fisheries management

title: A dedicated survey of fast-rotating near-Earth asteroids with the Two-meter Twin Telescope. II. Tumblers
abstractText: Fast rotation dominates the metre- to decametre-size near-Earth asteroid (NEA) population, but the incidence of non-principal-axis (NPA) rotation, or tumbling, in this regime is essentially unconstrained. We establish how common NPA rotation is among small, fast-rotating NEAs, how its prevalence varies with size, and what it implies for the internal structure and recent dynamical history of these bodies. We analysed the homogeneous high-cadence sample obtained with the Two-meter Twin Telescope at Teide Observatory and presented in the first paper of this series. Light curves showing coherent residual structure under a single-frequency Fourier model were refitted with a bivariate Fourier series in two independent frequencies, and dynamical modes were assigned from the normalised harmonic amplitude spectrum. We confirm 32 NPA rotators, 14 with both periods reliably resolved, with periods spanning 0.48--46.4 min and estimated diameters of 7--140 m. The most extreme object with both periods resolved, 2025 FB8 (shortest period P_1 = 71 s, estimated diameter D ≃ 7 m), is the fastest and smallest such tumbler characterised to date. Eight objects satisfy our harmonic quality criteria, and all eight are consistent with long-axis mode rotation. The tumbler fraction among fast rotators is 16.0%, rising from 13.8% at absolute magnitude H < 26 to 22.5% at H ≥ 26. Twenty-three of the 32 lie above the spin limit of a cohesionless rubble pile; none exceeds the lunar-regolith limit. Tumbling is common among small fast rotators, with no evidence that it becomes rarer towards the smallest sizes. Fast tumblers require modest cohesion but no monolithic interior, occupying the same structural domain as their principal-axis counterparts.

title: An aerodynamic panel method and mesh generator for educational and research applications in aerodynamics of aircraft design
abstractText: The open-source aerodynamic panel tool is a rapid and efficient tool for estimating aerodynamic characteristics, particularly during several phases of aircraft design; however, the accessibility of transparent, adaptable, user-friendly, and open-source aerodynamic tools suitable for educational and research environments remains challenging. This paper introduces Aircraft Panel Generation and Aerodynamic Analysis, an educational open-source software designed to provide easy access to aerodynamic analysis tools for aircraft studies. The software incorporates implementations of the Vortex Lattice Method and Doublet Lattice Method to compute steady and unsteady loads using the Aerodynamic Influence Coefficient matrices for compressible subsonic flows. The framework features advanced panel generation that discretizes lifting surface configurations into structured chordwise and spanwise trapezoidal elements. The accuracy of the code is demonstrated by validation against data from a published German Aerospace Center technical report across both steady and unsteady aerodynamic cases. The results show that the computed pressure coefficients are in good agreement with reference solutions. The example aircraft models are analyzed and visualized as illustrative examples. This software could serve as a valuable resource for academics and researchers, providing a foundation for further aeroelastic studies.

Socio-demographic Factors and Dietary Practices Associated with Overweight and Overfat Nutritional Status among Kyambogo University Students in Uganda
abstractText: Globally, the prevalence of non communicable diseases is rising, with overweight and obesity as major contributors, particularly among young adults. However, evidence on predictors of overweight, overfat, and obesity among young adults in resource-constrained settings remains limited, despite links to unhealthy dietary patterns established in early life. This study assessed socio-demographic factors and dietary practices associated with overweight and overfat, nutritional status among Kyambogo university students in Uganda. A cross-sectional study was conducted among 273 undergraduate students selected through convenience sampling. Quantitative data were collected using structured questionnaires capturing socio-demographic characteristics, dietary practices, lifestyle behaviors, and nutritional status. Qualitative data were obtained through six focus group discussions and six in-depth interviews. Quantitative data were analyzed using chi-square tests and binary logistic regression in SPSS version 20, while qualitative data were analyzed thematically. Nutritional status was determined using BMI and TBF% indicators based on WHO (2004) and TANITA cut-offs. Most participants were aged 18-23 years, with more females (190) than males (83). The prevalence of overweight and overfat was 20.1% and 46.2%, respectively. Overweight (defined here as including both overweight and obesity) was significantly associated with sex (p = 0.004) and marital status (p = 0.004). Male students had 69.3% lower odds of being overweight than female students (OR = 0.307). Likewise, single students had 83.8% lower odds of being overweight than married students (OR = 0.162). Students who routinely skipped breakfast were 3.3 times more likely to be overweight, and 2.2 times more likely to be overfat than those who consumed breakfast regularly. Usual breakfast consumption was significantly associated with both overweight (p = 0.005) and overfat status (p < 0.001). Overfat status was also associated with consuming fewer than three meals per day (p = 0.014), and perceptions of meal preparation costs (p = 0.032). Female students more frequently consumed deep-fried snacks (p = 0.002), and unhealthy combinations of deep-fried snacks and soda (p = 0.016). Weekly alcohol consumption was significantly associated with both overweight (p=0.043) and overfat (p=0.045). Qualitative findings revealed these unhealthy dietary practices were driven by financial limitations, time constraints, and limited access to affordable healthy foods on and around campus. In conclusion, overweight and overfat are prevalent among Kyambogo university students in Uganda, particulary among females and married students. These are influenced by socio-demographic and modifiable dietary factors. Targeted interventions, including nutrition education, improved access to affordable healthy foods, and supportive campus food environments, are needed to promote optimal nutritional status in this population. title: Numeracy Skills, Performance and Learning Challenges of Student-Athletes: A Mathematical Proficiency Analysis
abstractText: This study examined the numeracy skills, mathematical performance, and learning challenges of student-athletes in the CAMAG District, Schools Division of Bohol, during the school year 2025–2026, as a basis for developing a proposed action plan to enhance mathematical proficiency. A quantitative descriptive-correlational research design was employed, involving 100 student-athletes who qualified for provincial athletic competitions, comprising 61 junior high school and 39 senior high school students, with 30 mathematics teachers serving as coaches. Data were gathered using modified survey questionnaires and analyzed through descriptive statistics and chi-square tests of association at the 0.05 significance level. Findings revealed that student-athletes generally demonstrated satisfactory numeracy skills in accuracy (M = 2.76), speed and efficiency (M = 2.60), comprehension (M = 2.71), and application (M = 2.55), while confidence obtained the lowest mean (M = 2.49). Mathematical performance was predominantly satisfactory, with 45% obtaining grades of 80–84, followed by 38% obtaining grades of 75–79. Learning challenges registered an overall mean of 3.02, with difficulties remembering mathematical formulas and solving multistep problems among the major concerns. No significant associations were found between mathematical performance and selected demographic characteristics. However, significant associations were established between mathematical performance and learning challenges (χ² = 106.521, p < .001) and between numeracy skills and learning challenges (χ² = 58.760, p < .001). The study recommends targeted numeracy interventions, structured problem-solving activities, confidence-building strategies, and coordinated academic support for student-athletes.

Rethinking English Education In The Era Of Generative Ai And Global Englishes
abstractText: The advent of generative AI has provoked an ontological crisis in language education, tempting policymakers to equate machine-generated output with human interpretive capacity. This article challenges the premise that such technologies render language learning obsolete, arguing instead that an AI-saturated landscape makes robust humanistic engagement more vital than ever. Addressing the “scholar’s dilemma,” the paper proposes a structural shift in higher education from traditional silos toward horizontal, cross-disciplinary integration. Because English functions as a global lingua franca (ELF) and exerts an algorithmic hegemony over large language models (LLMs), advanced proficiency remains indispensable for critically querying these platforms. We advocate for a pedagogical evolution from the mechanical transmission of referential information (informing) to facilitating imaginative exploration (engaging). Central to this shift is the reclamation of “literature with a small l” as the primary representational material used to cultivate students’ “textual power.” By prioritizing the interpretive struggle over cognitive offloading—a tension described here as the “Picasso Paradox”—educators can formalize a “fifth skill” (complex critical thinking in English). This framework provides the cognitive foundation for students to navigate an AI-saturated world not as passive users, but as active curators equipped with ethical discernment and epistemic agency.

title: Causal associations with schizophrenia risk: a literature review and Mendelian randomization analysis
abstractText: Abstract Background Schizophrenia is a leading cause of worldwide disability, but there remains considerable uncertainty regarding its underlying causes. We aimed to conduct a systematic Mendelian randomization (MR) analysis to identify risk factors for schizophrenia. Methods We first conducted an extensive literature review of meta-analyses and previous MR studies to pinpoint potential risk factors for schizophrenia. Out of 213 candidates, we selected 85 factors with available genetic instrumental variables for MR analyses. Summary-level data for schizophrenia (76,755 cases and 243,649 controls) were obtained from the Psychiatric Genomics Consortium. A comprehensive two-sample MR analysis was performed to assess the causal relationships. Results We identified robust causal associations between six risk factors and schizophrenia, which remained consistent across stringent sensitivity analyses. Specifically, genetically predicted bipolar disorder (OR IVW =1.49, 95% CI: 1.41 to 1.58, P = 1.53 × 10 − 44 ), major depressive disorder (OR IVW =1.57, 95% CI: 1.36 to 1.82, P = 1.31 × 10 − 9 ), worry sub-cluster (OR IVW =1.45, 95% CI: 1.08 to 1.95, P = 0.01), and the number of sexual partners (OR IVW =1.97, 95% CI: 1.62 to 2.39, P = 8.72 × 10 − 12 ) were significantly associated with an increased risk of schizophrenia. Conversely, higher cognitive abilities demonstrated robust protective effects, specifically intelligence quotient (OR IVW =0.82, 95% CI: 0.72 to 0.93, P = 1.91 × 10 − 3 ) and executive function (OR IVW =0.29, 95% CI: 0.19 to 0.45, P = 2.81 × 10 − 8 ). Crucially, reverse MR analyses revealed significant bidirectional effects across all six traits, demonstrating that genetic liability to schizophrenia also causally drives cognitive deterioration and exacerbates these psychiatric and behavioral vulnerabilities. Conclusion Our study evaluated 85 potential risk factors and established robust bidirectional causal associations between six core traits and schizophrenia. Ultimately, these findings emphasize that early cognitive remediation and proactive management of comorbid affective disorders are crucial to disrupt the mutually reinforcing cycle of schizophrenia progression. title: DisCoTune-mediated co-expression enhances functional hSOD1 production in Escherichia coli
abstractText: Human Copper/Zinc (Cu/Zn) superoxide dismutase 1 (hSOD1) is a cytosolic antioxidant enzyme that requires disulfide formation and metal incorporation to achieve catalytic activity. However, production of disulfide bond containing protein in Escherichia coli (E. coli) is hindered by the bacterial cytosol's limited capacity for these maturation steps, resulting in insoluble or inactive protein. To address this, a recombinant hSOD1 was expressed in a standard bacterial expression strain and compared to co-expression using a tunable auxiliary plasmid system, DisCoTune (Disulphide bond formation in E. coli with tunable expression), that increases cytoplasmic oxidative folding capacity under adjustable promoters. The cultures were supplemented with copper and zinc, and the protein was purified by affinity capture followed by size-exclusion chromatography. In enzyme activity assay, the tunable co-expression strategy significantly improving specific enzyme activity of the recombinant hSOD1. This resulted in the recombinant protein with significantly higher specific activity (61203 U/mg) compared to the standard expression protocol.

Explainable radiogenomic neural networks for molecular risk stratification in clear cell renal cell carcinoma: a single-center study with a descriptive breast cancer workflow stress test
abstractText: Background Clear cell renal cell carcinoma exhibits substantial molecular heterogeneity, and clinically relevant alterations involving BAP1, SETD2, the PI3K/AKT/mTOR signaling pathway, and hypoxia-related protein-expression profiles may not be fully captured by conventional imaging interpretation. Radiogenomic neural networks may support non-invasive molecular risk stratification; however, limited explainability, small validation cohorts, and uncertain transportability remain important obstacles. Objective This study developed an explainable radiogenomic neural network for molecular high-risk stratification in clear cell renal cell carcinoma and secondarily evaluated a separate breast cancer cohort only as a descriptive workflow stress test. Methods This retrospective single-center exploratory study enrolled 210 patients treated between January 2019 and December 2025. The primary renal cohort comprised 150 patients with clear cell renal cell carcinoma and was chronologically divided into a development set, an internal validation set, and a small temporal test set. A separate cohort of 60 patients with invasive breast cancer was retained only as a secondary descriptive workflow stress test. Because the breast image-risk score generation workflow could not be reliably reconstructed, the breast analysis was not treated as external validation or a reproducible renal-to-breast model-transfer experiment. The renal molecular high-risk endpoint was a prespecified composite of BAP1 protein loss, high P4HA3 expression using a development-set-fixed cutoff, pathogenic or likely pathogenic alterations in BAP1 or SETD2, or pathogenic/likely pathogenic alterations involving the mTOR signaling pathway. Endpoint-defining variables were excluded from predictors. A three-dimensional convolutional neural network generated the image risk score and represents the fully documented primary predictive model in the present revision. Archived combined risk scores that integrated the image risk score with prespecified non-endpoint variables were retained only as a secondary exploratory analysis because the estimator-level fusion operator and associated scaling/encoding details could not be completely reconstructed from the archived materials. Grad-CAM and SHAP were used as post hoc explanation methods. Results Molecular high-risk status was identified in 43 of 150 renal patients (28.7%), including 32/105 (30.5%) in the development set, 8/30 (26.7%) in internal validation, and 3/15 (20.0%) in the temporal test set. In renal internal validation, the fully documented image-only 3D CNN achieved an AUC of 0.756; the secondary archived combined-model AUC was 0.801. In the renal temporal test set, the image-only AUC was 0.750 and the secondary combined-model AUC was 0.639; because this set contained only 15 patients and 3 high-risk events, these estimates were considered exploratory. Threshold-based classification metrics and calibration statistics for the primary image-only 3D CNN could not be reliably reconstructed from the archived case-level materials and therefore are not reported. In the breast workflow stress-test cohort, the image-risk AUC was 0.652 and the archived combined-score AUC was 0.649. Because the breast image-risk score generation workflow could not be reliably reconstructed, breast performance was retained only as descriptive technical stress-test output and not as evidence of a reproducible renal-to-breast model-transfer experiment. Conclusion An explainable radiogenomic 3D CNN showed measurable discrimination for molecular high-risk status in clear cell renal cell carcinoma during internal validation. The image-only model is the principal reproducibly documented predictive model in this revision, whereas the archived combined-model outputs are retained as secondary exploratory analyses because the exact estimator-level fusion implementation could not be fully reconstructed. Numerically different performance in the 15-patient temporal test set should be regarded as exploratory because only three high-risk events were present, and the estimates may be sensitive to the single development split and initialization. The breast analysis was retained only as a descriptive technical stress test because its image-risk score generation workflow could not be reliably reconstructed; it was not considered external validation of renal cancer biology or a reproducible model-transfer experiment. Larger multicenter cohorts with repeated model refitting, complete prospective archiving of model specifications, and prospective testing are required before clinical translation.

title: Teaching Performance in a Rural Elementary School: Basis for a Teaching Enhancement Plan
abstractText: This study assessed the teaching performance of teachers at Guba Elementary School during School Year 2025–2026 to develop a Teaching Enhancement Plan. Specifically, it examined respondents' profiles in terms of age, gender, highest educational attainment, teaching position, years of teaching experience, and the number of trainings and seminars attended. It also determined their level of teaching performance across the six Key Result Areas (KRAs), identified their priority area for professional enhancement, and examined the relationship between their profile and overall teaching performance. A quantitative descriptive-correlational design was employed with 30 teacher-respondents, using a questionnaire adapted from the Individual Performance Commitment and Review Form (IPCRF) and analyzed using descriptive and inferential statistics. Findings showed an overall Outstanding level of teaching performance (M = 4.63, SD = 0.25), with Learning Environment rated highest (M = 4.80) and Assessment and Reporting lowest (M = 4.41). In the priority ranking, Assessment and Reporting was identified by 10 respondents (33.33%) as the highest priority area for professional enhancement, followed by Personal Growth and Professional Development (9 respondents, 30.00%) and Curriculum and Planning (6 respondents, 20.00%); Learning Environment was ranked first by 3 respondents (10.00%), while Content Knowledge and Pedagogy and Diversity of Learners each received one vote (3.33%). Furthermore, years of teaching experience demonstrated a significant moderate positive relationship with overall teaching performance (Spearman rho = 0.489, p = 0.006), while the remaining profile variables showed no significant relationships. Based on these findings, the study proposed a Teaching Enhancement Plan to strengthen teachers' competencies in assessment practices, professional development, and curriculum planning, supporting continuous professional growth and sustaining teachers' existing level of performance.

Bad food, good stories: negative memorable ethnic food experiences of international travelers
abstractText: Purpose This study aims to explore how international travelers experience, manage and retrospectively narrate negative memorable experiences with ethnic food, and to identify their components and structure. Design/methodology/approach Applying the Expectancy Disconfirmation Theory and Negativity Bias Theory, this qualitative research utilized reflexive thematic analysis on 27 in-depth interviews with international travelers. Findings As a result of the analysis, four major themes were generated: sensory and physical betrayal, expectation violation, in situ social performance of tolerance and retrospective narrative transformation. Findings confirm that NMFTEs are complex events rooted in expectation failure and amplified by negativity bias. Critically, the study introduces empathetic contextualization, a novel cognitive-affective process where tourists actively reframe negative experiences as anecdotes or learning opportunities, thereby preventing destination-level devaluation. Practical implications This research refines existing theories and provides practical implications for destination managers. Originality/value To the authors' knowledge, this is among the first studies to examine negative memorable food experiences in ethnic food consumption, an area dominated by positive-centric research. The study contributes a four-theme structure of these experiences, extends Expectancy Disconfirmation (ED) and Negativity Bias theories by showing how social context shapes both in-the-moment responses and later remembering, and introduces empathetic contextualization as a process that protects destination image.

title: The Digital Contagion of Misinformation: Simulation of Critical Propagation Thresholds in Social Networks
abstractText: Misinformation propagation on social networks can intensify when individual sharing decisions generate collective cascades. This study aimed to examine the influence of activation thresholds on the final reach and temporal evolution of this process through computational simulation. An irreversible threshold model was implemented on Erdős–Rényi random networks comprising 1,000 users, an average degree of ten, and 5% initially active users. One hundred repetitions were performed per scenario. Thresholds from 0.10 to 0.50 were evaluated, followed by a finer analysis of the transition region. Mean reach dropped from 88.26% to 8.25% as the threshold increased from 0.250 to 0.255; the frequency of extensive cascades decreased from 87% to 1%. These findings reveal an abrupt transition governed by the activation rule and the structure of the simulated network, without implying a universal threshold for real-world platforms.

Socioecological Influences on Food and Nutrition Security Among Publicly Insured Families
abstractText: BACKGROUND Understanding of the factors influencing food and nutrition security among households with children remains limited, particularly during pediatric hospitalization, a vulnerable period for food access. Caregivers’ perspectives offer critical insights into the determinants of food-related decision-making and the strategies households use to obtain preferred, nutritious foods. METHODS We conducted a qualitative study using semistructured interviews with caregivers of publicly insured hospitalized children from an existing study cohort. We purposively sampled participants using maximal variation sampling to reflect a range of food and nutrition security statuses. Guided by a socioecological framework, interviews explored caregivers’ perspectives on nutrition, food access and benefits, and community resources. Transcripts were analyzed using thematic analysis with both inductive and deductive coding, informed by the same framework. RESULTS We interviewed 23 caregivers, predominantly from food-secure and nutrition-secure households. Six themes were identified, including (1) balancing nutritional ideals with everyday realities; (2) dynamics of food access across cycles of resource fluctuation and strain; (3) dignity, choice, and a hierarchy with food assistance programs; (4) food scarcity–driven sacrifice, emotional burden, and adaptive measures; (5) technology-enabled strategies to mitigate barriers to food access and nutrition information; and (6) skepticism toward the food system and a preference for natural foods. CONCLUSION Constrained choices, fluctuating resources, and system-level factors shaped perceptions of food and nutrition, influencing caregivers’ sense of dignity, control, and adaptive strategies, such as using grocery-delivery services and online sources. These findings highlight the importance of autonomy and stability in supporting vulnerable families’ access to preferred foods.

title: The Effect of Storage Conditions on the Viability and Antagonistic Activity of Lactobacillus delbrueckii subsp. Bulgaricus 1Z 03501 Culture Immobilized in Alginate-Pectin Films Following Lyophilization
abstractText: The aim of the study was to evaluate the viability, antagonistic and cultural properties of the probiotic strain Lactobacillus delbrueckii subsp. bulgaricus 1Z 03501, immobilized in alginate-pectin films with the addition of a protective sucrose-milk-lactose medium (APF SML) or saline solution (APF SS), following freeze-drying and subsequent storage at temperatures of 4 and –20 °C for three months. The lactobacilli were immobilized in films based on a 3% sodium alginate solution and a 3% pectin solution in appropriate proportions, cross-linked by calcium ions, and cultured in Blaurock’s medium for 48 hours. The samples were frozen to –28 °C, followed by vacuum drying with a residual pressure in the chamber not exceeding 50 Pa. Upon completion of the drying process, the samples were placed in airtight polyethylene vacuum bags and transferred to refrigerators and freezers for storage at temperatures of 4 and –20 °C. The titer of viable cells was determined by the serial dilution method after dissolving the films in sodium citrate. Antagonistic activity was assessed against Pseudomonas aeruginosa 9027 based on the width of the growth inhibition zones. Cultural properties were determined visually in Blaurock’s semi-solid medium. It was found that prior to lyophilization, the number of viable lactobacilli cells in the APF SS sample was 9.14 lg CFU/g, and the number of viable cells in the APF SML samples was 8.67 lg CFU/g. Following lyophilization, this figure decreased by 2.17 and 1.57 lg CFU/g, respectively. After the first month of storage at 4 °C, the titer of viable cells decreased by 0.75 lg CFU/g in the APP FR samples and by 0.48 lg CFU/g in the APF SML samples. Subsequently, as the storage period was extended to 3 months at 4 °C, a significant loss in the number of viable cells was observed in the test samples. The viability index of APF SS decreased by 3.37 lg CFU/g, whilst in APP SML samples it decreased by 2.36 lg CFU/g compared with the data obtained immediately after lyophilization. Storage at –20 °C ensured better preservation of the immobilized probiotic culture. The viability indices for APF SS and APF SML after one month of storage were 6.68 and 7.08 lg CFU/g, respectively. After 3 months’ storage under the above conditions, the number of viable cells in the APF SS and APF SML samples decreased by 2.45 and 1.93 lg CFU/g, respectively, compared with the data obtained immediately after lyophilization. Throughout the entire observation period, the films inhibited the growth of the test culture Pseudomonas aeruginosa strain 9027, whilst the cultural properties remained unchanged regardless of the storage conditions and duration. The results of the studies indicate that freeze-dried alginate-pectin films containing the immobilized probiotic culture Lactobacillus delbrueckii subsp. bulgaricus 1Z 03501 retain their viability and antagonistic activity for at least 3 months. It has been shown that storage at a temperature of -20 °C ensures better preservation, whilst the SML protective medium reduces the loss of viable cells during storage.

title: Beyond Current Efforts: A Critical Look At Reducing Disability Discrimination
abstractText: This study examined current efforts to address discrimination against individuals with disabilities. Participants were asked to complete the survey to provide examples of any ongoing relevant initiatives and assess each initiative on its effectiveness, beneficence, and continuance. The findings indicated thirteen major themes in participants’ responses: Accessibility; Accommodation; Awareness/Advocacy; Content Reading; Equity; Inclusive Education; Employment; Legislation; Media Representation; Open Discussion; Perception/Attitude; Technology; Training. The study underscores a pressing need to continuously monitor, reassess, and readjust current efforts to address disability discrimination, and to apply a critical evaluation to each initiative in terms of effectiveness, beneficence, and continuation moving forward.

Comparative physiological responses to self-paced exercise in men across age–training status: effort distribution, cerebral–muscle oxygenation and neuromuscular performance
abstractText: Abstract To compare self-paced cycling performance, effort distribution, and associated neuromuscular and physiological responses across three age–training phenotypes. Twenty-eight healthy men were classified as young trained (YT, n = 8; 26.3 ± 6.9 y), older trained (OT, n = 11; 57.5 ± 3.4 y), or young untrained (YU, n = 9; 24.8 ± 5.3 y). Participants completed a 25-min self-paced cycling time trial comprising five 4.5-min lower-intensity sections, each followed by a 30-s maximal sprint. Power output, heart rate (HR), rating of perceived exertion, blood lactate, core and skin temperature, cerebral and muscle tissue oxygenation, and pre/post knee-extensor neuromuscular function were assessed. Total distance differed between groups ( P = 0.037), with OT cycling further than YU (12.87 ± 1.32 vs. 11.48 ± 0.89 km; mean difference 1.40 km, 95% CI 0.35–2.44; adjusted P = 0.035), whereas OT and YT did not differ. During lower-intensity sections, OT produced greater absolute power than YU (mean difference 51.8 W, 95% CI 18.8–84.7; adjusted P = 0.012). Sprint-power variability was lower in OT than YU (7.8 ± 6.0 vs. 28.4 ± 18.5%; adjusted P = 0.030). Peak HR was lower in OT than both younger groups. Voluntary activation showed no significant group x time interaction ( P = 0.062), and NIRS responses showed no significant group x stage interactions. Older trained men achieved self-paced cycling performance comparable with young trained men and greater than young untrained men, characterised by sustained lower-intensity power and more stable sprint output despite a lower peak HR.

title: SEGURANÇA DO PACIENTE NO CENTRO CIRÚRGICO: ATUAÇÃO DA ENFERMAGEM NA UTILIZAÇÃO DO CHECKLIST DE CIRURGIA SEGURA
abstractText: A atuação da enfermagem na aplicação do Checklist de Cirurgia Segura integra as práticas de segurança do paciente no centro cirúrgico. Este estudo tem como objetivo analisar essa atuação, considerando as verificações realizadas, as dificuldades de aplicação e as estratégias de melhoria. Trata-se de um estudo bibliográfico desenvolvido a partir de levantamento exploratório de publicações de 2020 a 2026, com síntese descritiva e comparativa de seis estudos diretamente relacionados à temática. As informações foram organizadas em quadro contendo autoria, ano, objetivo, método e principais resultados. Os achados evidenciam participação relevante da enfermagem na condução das verificações e na comunicação entre os profissionais, acompanhada de diferenças no cumprimento dos itens e das etapas do instrumento. Entre as dificuldades, destacam-se insegurança profissional, limitações na capacitação, cooperação multiprofissional insuficiente e problemas de organização do trabalho. Educação permanente, definição de rotinas e acompanhamento da execução constituem estratégias apontadas para aprimorar sua utilização. Conclui-se que a contribuição da enfermagem se fortalece quando a aplicação do checklist combina preparo técnico, suporte institucional e participação da equipe. A implantação do instrumento requer avaliação contínua das verificações, consolidando a segurança cirúrgica como responsabilidade compartilhada.

abstractText: Kecemasan pra anestesi merupakan salah satu respons psikologis yang dapat dialami pasien sebelum menjalani tindakan pembedahan dengan anestesi umum. Kondisi tersebut dapat memengaruhi respons fisiologis dan psikologis pasien serta berhubungan dengan pengalaman nyeri setelah operasi. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk mengetahui hubungan antara kecemasan pra anestesi dengan nyeri pasca anestesi umum di Rumah Sakit Umum Daerah Batara Siang Pangkep. Penelitian ini menggunakan metode kuantitatif dengan desain analitik korelasional dan pendekatan cross-sectional. Teknik pengambilan sampel menggunakan total sampling dengan jumlah responden sebanyak 90 orang. Analisis data dilakukan secara univariat dan bivariat menggunakan uji korelasi Spearman Rank. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa terdapat hubungan positif yang signifikan antara kecemasan pra anestesi dengan nyeri pasca anestesi umum. Hasil uji Spearman Rank memperoleh nilai koefisien korelasi sebesar 0,511 dengan nilai signifikansi p < 0,001. Hal ini menunjukkan adanya hubungan positif dengan kekuatan korelasi kuat antara kecemasan pra anestesi dan nyeri pasca anestesi umum. Kesimpulan penelitian ini adalah terdapat hubungan yang signifikan antara kecemasan pra anestesi dengan nyeri pasca anestesi umum di Rumah Sakit Umum Daerah Batara Siang Pangkep. Oleh karena itu, penilaian kecemasan sebelum tindakan anestesi perlu diperhatikan sebagai bagian dari upaya meningkatkan pelayanan dan kenyamanan pasien.

title: Multiscale Interface Engineering of Nickel–Iron Alloy/Sulfide-Based Integral Self-Supporting Electrode for Seawater Electrolysis and Enrofloxacin Electrochemical Sensing
abstractText: Abstract The interface of electrochemically active materials serves as an important medium for electrochemical reactions, and the construction of multiple and cross-scale interfaces is the key to enhancing reaction activity. Herein, based on the ligand-assisted spatial confinement strategy, dispersed heterogeneous crystalline domains composed of nickel–iron alloys and nickel–iron bimetallic sulfides were constructed under the calcination condition and anchored in situ onto a nitrogen and sulfur codoped two-dimensional carbon network, thereby forming an electrocatalytically active substance with multiple heterogeneous interfaces. Subsequently, it was attached to the nickel foam support through the adhesion of biopolymers to form an integral self-supporting electrode. At the microscopic scale, the strong electronic coupling at the interface between the alloy/dual-metal sulfide/carbon matrix enriched the catalytic sites and regulated the mass transfer of reactants and the adsorption of reaction intermediates. At the macroscopic scale, the electrochemical active substance formed a superhydrophilic/superaerophobic wetting interface on the surface of the nickel foam, improving bubble separation and electrolyte permeation. The synergy of these interface characteristics simultaneously endowed the catalyst with dual functions of electrolyzing seawater and sensing the antibiotic enrofloxacin. In alkaline simulated seawater electrolysis, regardless of the oxygen or hydrogen evolution reaction, a current density of 1000 mA·cm–2 was achieved with a relatively low overpotential, and it could maintain long-term stable operation in the overall water-splitting process. As a sensor, this integral self-supporting electrode was directly used, and it showed a wide linear range, extremely low detection limit, and excellent anti-interference ability for enrofloxacin. This work provides a compelling illustrative example for the design of multiscale interface structures of integral self-supporting electrodes with multifunctional electrochemical applications.

title: Comparative evaluation of integrated weed management strategies for sustainable sunflower production under field conditions in India
abstractText: Weeds that emerge early in the season limit sunflower ( Helianthus annuus L.) yields in India, and the rising cost and scarcity of farm labour have made repeated hand weeding increasingly uneconomical. Field experiments were conducted over three consecutive late monsoon (late kharif ) seasons (2023, 2024 and 2025) at the Zonal Agricultural Research Station, University of Agricultural Sciences, Bengaluru, Karnataka, India, under the All India Coordinated Research Project (AICRP) on Sunflower. Seven weed-management practices, comprising pre- and post-emergence herbicides, mechanical and manual weeding, the farmers’ practice, a weed-free check and a weedy check, were compared in a randomized complete block design with three replications. All treatments were imposed at a single wide-row spacing (75 × 25 cm), so row spacing itself was not an experimental factor. Pre-emergence pendimethalin (1.0 kg a.i. ha −1 ) followed by a directed post-emergence spray of quizalofop ethyl (62 g a.i. ha −1 ) at 15–20 days after sowing was the most effective practical treatment. Among the practical treatments, it recorded the lowest weed dry weight (41.3 g m −2 ) and the highest weed control efficiency (92.7%), and its seed yield (1646.3 kg ha −1 ) was statistically on par with the weed-free check (1730.7 kg ha −1 ) and about 53% higher than that of the farmers’ practice (1073.0 kg ha −1 ). Because it required less labour for weeding, it gave net returns close to those of the weed-free check and the highest benefit–cost ratio (2.6). Across treatment means, seed yield was positively associated with head diameter ( r = +0.78), consistent with a link between early-season weed control and reproductive sink size. We conclude that a sequential pre- and post-emergence herbicide programme can replace labour-intensive hand weeding in wide-row sunflower without a significant yield penalty and at a lower cost of cultivation. This option is recommended for sunflower growers in the semi-arid regions of southern India facing labour shortages, although it should be validated across other agro-climatic zones before wider adoption.

title: Interfacial Control of a GaN-Based High Electron Mobility Transistor via a SiN x Nanomask: From Wetting Dynamics to Breakdown Enhancement
abstractText: Abstract The controlled overgrowth of GaN on Si using a SiNx nanomask has attracted considerable attention, yet the relationship between the SiH4 precursor flux, interfacial growth kinetics, and device performance has not been fully established. Here, we employed pixel-wise spatial and spectral information from hyperspectral cathodoluminescence (HYP-CL) mapping to expose the SiH4 flow rate-mediated interfacial wetting/dewetting behavior of the SiNx nanomask that drastically affected the GaN nucleation kinetics at the SiNx/GaN interface. A low SiH4 flux induced wetting behavior, leading to a laterally extended SiNx nanomask, resulting in premature GaN island coalescence. Meanwhile, at a higher SiH4 flux, the observations are consistent with a wetting-to-dewetting behavioral transition, leading to aggregated SiNx clusters, resulting in vertically extended coalescence-free GaN pillars. Through this study, we unraveled the trade-off between cross-sectional film continuity and threading dislocation density suppression, which directly translates to the electrical performance. Also, we establish a design principle for nanomask engineering at semiconductor interfaces based on CL imaging for optimizing buffer layer design in high-voltage GaN-based devices.

Effects of Flowering Stage and Drying Method on the Bioactive Compounds and Antioxidant Activity of Opuntia stricta Flowers and Sensory Acceptability of a Citric-Acid-Pretreated Infusion
abstractText: The growing awareness of the role of nutrition in health promotion has increased consumer interest in beverages that are both refreshing and functional. Undervalued plant resources rich in bioactive compounds present opportunities for the development of novel functional foods and beverages. Opuntia stricta (OS) cactus flowers contain bioactive compounds, making them promising candidates for functional beverage development. This study evaluated the effects of flowering stage and drying methods: freeze-drying, oven-drying and solar-drying on the bioactive composition and in vitro antioxidant activity of Opuntia stricta flowers. It also assessed the sensory acceptability of an infusion prepared from citric-acid-pretreated, dried flowers. Total flavonoid content ranged from 410 to 5249 mg Quercetin Equivalent (QE)/100 g dry weight (DW), total phenolic content from 540 to 1534 mg Gallic Acid Equivalent (GAE)/100 g DW, total betalain content from 21 to 358 mg/100 g DW and anthocyanin content from 1033 to 2577 mg/100 g DW. 2,2-diphenyl-1-picrylhydrazyl (DPPH) radical scavenging activity (10 mg/mL) ranged from 4% to 81%. Flowering stage, drying method and their interaction significantly affected all measured parameters (p < 0.05). Freeze-drying consistently retained the highest levels of bioactive compounds and antioxidant activity across all flowering stages, whereas solar-drying resulted in the greatest losses. Anthesis flowers exhibited the highest levels of total phenolics, flavonoids, betalains and antioxidant activity, while anthocyanin content was highest at the budding stage. Despite the superior preservation achieved by freeze-drying, oven-drying was selected for product development due to its practicality, affordability and suitability for wider-scale application. The sensory analysis results showed that both 0.5% and 1% citric acid treatments improved the acceptability compared to the control, with the 1% treatment achieving the highest mean overall-liking score but was not significantly different from 0.5%. Overall, the findings demonstrate that harvesting the flowers of OS at anthesis and then oven-drying them could be a viable method for producing a beverage from this underutilized species. Pretreatment with citric acid improved the sensory acceptability, highlighting the potential of OS flowers for value addition. These findings highlight cactus flowers as promising sources of bioactive compounds for sustainable, locally relevant functional beverage development. Key words: Opuntia stricta, phytochemicals, antioxidant, infusion, sensory, bioactive, drying, functional beverage.

An explainable AI framework for integrated authentication, intrusion detection, and adaptive data transmission in IoMT networks
abstractText: Abstract Real-time monitoring, remote diagnostics, and automated medical treatments are all made possible by the Internet of Medical Things (IoMT), this has revolutionised healthcare. However, due of their improved connectivity, IoMT devices are more exposed to a range of cybersecurity attacks, such as malware insertion, spoofing, man-in-the-middle attacks, and distributed denial-of-service assaults. Traditional black-box AI models provide robust security mechanisms but lack transparency, making it difficult to identify and mitigate cyber threats effectively. This work introduces an explainable AI (XAI)-driven cybersecurity framework for IoMT applications to enhance trust, interpretability, and resilience against cyber threats. The proposed framework integrates deep learning networks with local model networks for authentication, employs a enhanced deep Q-Network for secure data transmission, and leverages XAI-based techniques for real-time attack detection and resistance. The model incorporates SHAP and LIME to provide interpretable security decisions, ensuring that IoMT stakeholders can understand and act on AI-generated security insights. In addition, this paper discusses a detailed attack resistance study using XAI, which shows the degree to which the proposed framework withstands various cyber threats.The paper evaluates security effectiveness metrics such as false positive rate, attack detection rate, response time, and the explainability score to judge the performance of XAI in IoMT security. Compared to conventional AI models, XAI-based detection accuracy has been proved to be significantly better experimentally, the reaction time was shortened, and the system was more transparent.

Associations between life-course cumulative moderate heat exposure and late-life memory decline in Europe
abstractText: Abstract Background Late-life memory decline is a major public health concern, yet the long-term association between life-course moderate heat exposure and memory decline remains unclear. Methods We analyzed 23,622 middle-aged and older adults from the SHARE study and linked retrospective life-course moderate heat exposure histories from the SHARE-ENV module with longitudinal memory assessments. Nonlinear exposure–response relationships and regional heterogeneity were examined using restricted cubic spline models. The predictive importance of exposure across life stages was assessed using random survival forests, and longitudinal memory trajectories were evaluated using linear mixed models. Exploratory mediation analyses further assessed potential biomarker-related pathways. Results In the primary Cox proportional hazards analyses, life-course moderate heat exposure showed substantial heterogeneity in its associations with late-life memory decline across regions and life stages. In Northern Europe, higher moderate heat exposure during middle adulthood was associated with a lower risk of memory decline (HR = 0.29, 95% CI: 0.20–0.42 per IQR increase), whereas the corresponding association in Central Europe indicated an increased risk (HR = 1.08, 95% CI: 1.02–1.15 per IQR increase). Restricted cubic spline analyses further revealed distinct nonlinear exposure–response patterns, characterized by inverse associations in Northern Europe, positive associations in Southern Europe, and threshold-like patterns in Central Europe. Linear mixed-effects models showed that individuals with higher moderate heat exposure trajectories experienced faster longitudinal memory decline (time-by-trajectory interaction: β = −0.008, SE = 0.002, p < 0.001 in Model 3). Random survival forest analyses ranked middle adulthood among the life stages with the highest predictive importance. Exploratory mediation analyses suggested that EGF-related pathways accounted for approximately 6.6% of the association between moderate heat exposure and memory decline. Conclusions Cumulative moderate heat exposure across the life course was associated with late-life memory decline, with exposure during middle adulthood showing relatively high predictive importance. These findings suggest that moderate heat exposure may represent an underrecognized environmental factor related to healthy memory aging under climate change.

title: Conformal La2O3 Interphase Regulates CEI Formation and Buffers Lattice Strain in 4.6 V LiCoO2 Cathodes
abstractText: Abstract Unlocking the high-voltage capability of LiCoO2 (LCO) is critical for next-generation high-energy lithium-ion batteries (LIBs), yet batteries cycled above 4.5 V suffer from an unstable cathode–electrolyte interphase (CEI), electrolyte corrosion, and lattice degradation. Herein, a conformal nano-La2O3 interphase is fabricated on LCO to regulate CEI formation and buffer lattice strain at 4.6 V. Different from inert coatings, the chemically active La2O3 interphase neutralizes HF from electrolyte decomposition and suppresses cobalt dissolution. In situ XRD verifies relieved anisotropic lattice fluctuation during Li+ (de)intercalation. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations show that surface electronic reconstruction reduces the Li+ diffusion barrier from 1.50 to 1.05 eV and inhibits parasitic side reactions, while finite element simulations (FES) confirm homogenized local current and mitigated chemo-mechanical stress. Post-mortem characterizations demonstrate the formation of a thin, uniform CEI and restrained oxygen release. Owing to synergistic protection, La2O3@LCO delivers an initial charge capacity of 233.45 mAh g–1 at 0.1 C and 77% retention after 300 cycles at 0.5 C (4.6 V cut-off). This work provides insights into functional interphase design for durable high-voltage layered oxide cathodes.

Real-Time Academic Platform Integration Design (RAPID): A Descriptive Framework for Course Communication and Support
abstractText: Abstract Persistent, channel-organized communication environments give instructors ways to arrange questions, assistance, announcements, and informal interaction alongside a learning management system. Their use depends on how students enter the environment, how information and audiences are organized, who provides assistance, and how participation is experienced. This conceptual article presents Real-Time Academic Platform Integration Design (RAPID), a descriptive framework developed through a focused synthesis of 37 publications and a source-anchored matrix of 750 evidence items. Following a bounded literature search with artificial intelligence support for screening and extraction, the authors reviewed source evidence and selected and refined the framework by comparing model-generated alternatives. RAPID comprises four components: Student Onboarding, Environment Organization, Sustainable Help, and Student Participation and Social Climate, interpreted through an affordance perspective and Community of Inquiry. A constructed LMS-centered baseline, two reflective teaching illustrations, and a literature-informed projection show how it applies across differences in course size, staffing, and participation requirements. The framework’s usefulness, workload implications, and relationship to learning require empirical study.

Advanced three-dimensional bioprinting for in vitro tumor model engineering: From biomimetic model construction to personalized precision medicine
abstractText: Three-dimensional (3D) bioprinting technology offers a transformative approach for constructing biomimetic tumor organoid models that overcome the limitations of traditional two-dimensional cell cultures and animal models. This review systematically summarizes recent advances in 3D bioprinted tumor organoids, emphasizing extrusion-based, inkjet-based, and lithography-based bioprinting methods. These technologies enable precise spatial control of cell distribution and tissue architecture, achieving high reproducibility while maintaining complex tumor microenvironmental characteristics. Applications across multiple cancer types—including colorectal, gastric, pancreatic, breast, glioma, renal, bladder, lung, and thyroid cancers—demonstrate significant potential for drug screening, tumor heterogeneity research, and preclinical evaluation of individualized treatment responses. Despite substantial progress, challenges remain regarding multicellular complexity simulation, technical resolution, and biomaterial optimization. Future directions include integrating four-dimensional bioprinting, multiomics analysis, and immune microenvironment reconstruction to enhance physiological fidelity and clinical applicability, ultimately advancing precision oncology and personalized cancer treatment strategies.

title: Towards a Pedagogical Framework for Integrating Generative AI Into Competency-Based Education in Secondary Schools in the Global South
abstractText: Secondary education systems across the Global South have adopted competency-based curricula that expect learners to construct knowledge, solve authentic problems, collaborate and demonstrate skills, yet large classes, teacher shortages and limited resources constrain the learner-centered pedagogy that these reforms require. Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) has been proposed as a means of closing this gap, but its pedagogical role in competency-based education has not been systematically theorized. Guided by Vygotsky’s social constructivist theory, this study synthesized peer-reviewed and institutional literature published between 2015 and 2025 through a systematic review of 300 sources, selected from 12,125 Scopus and Web of Science records and reported according to the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) 2020. The study found that competency-based reforms were constrained by teacher preparation, assessment practices and resources. GenAI offered affordances for scaffolding, dialogue, feedback, authentic task design and teacher support, and randomized trials in Nigeria and Ghana reported meaningful learning gains when GenAI tutoring was structured and supervised. However, unguided access was associated with overreliance and weaker independent performance, and connectivity, language, cost, teacher capacity and policy gaps constrained equitable use. The study proposes the Scaffolded Generative AI for Competency-Based Education (SGAI-CBE) framework, which organizes GenAI use into a six-phase pedagogical cycle anchored in the zone of proximal development, teacher-mediated scaffolding, collaborative knowledge construction, authentic assessment and the gradual fading of AI support, and situates the cycle within enabling conditions and guardrails appropriate for resource-constrained schools.

Constructing and Implementing an Integrated Model of Tiered Instruction and ESP for College English
abstractText: The marked individual differences among learners and the insufficient cultivation of language application ability are long-standing problems in College English teaching at application-oriented undergraduate universities in China. Existing reforms have usually treated tiered instruction and English for Specific Purposes (ESP) as two independent measures: tiering is implemented at the teaching-management level, while ESP is added as a separate course. Neither has addressed the fundamental issue of differentiating course content. Drawing on differentiated instruction, needs-analysis-based ESP course design, and blended learning, this study constructs and implements an integrated model that combines offline tiered College English with online tiered ESP courses. With differentiation, disciplinary alignment, and process orientation as its guiding principles, the model organizes online ESP courses for two proficiency tiers (A and B) by discipline cluster and incorporates a multi-dimensional assessment mechanism. Three preliminary observations are presented. First, without corresponding differentiation in course content, tiering remains formal. Second, online ESP courses provide a bridge linking English instruction with disciplinary training and impose higher interdisciplinary requirements on teachers. Third, platform-based records provide a foundation for implementing process-oriented assessment. The model can serve as a design-level reference for application-oriented undergraduate institutions seeking to advance the integration of tiered instruction and ESP.

title: Hidden parasites in diatom blooms: high infection rates of Leptocylindrus danicus by the oomycete Miracula nipponica
abstractText: Abstract Parasitic fungi and fungal-like organisms are increasingly recognized as key players influencing diatom dynamics and carbon fluxes in aquatic ecosystems; however, their diversity and ecological roles in coastal environments remain poorly understood. Here, we investigated the diversity of fungi and fungal-like organisms over an annual cycle, encompassing spring diatom blooms, in Sagami Bay, Japan, using 18S rDNA metabarcoding, and quantified parasitic infection of diatoms during the spring bloom of May 2022 using fluorescence microscopy and single-spore PCR. The composition of fungi and fungal-like organisms exhibited pronounced seasonal and vertical variations, and the relative read abundances of Chytridiomycota and Oomycota increased during diatom bloom periods. We found that the oomycete Miracula nipponica , recently described from Sagami Bay, infected the bloom-forming diatom Leptocylindrus danicus during the spring bloom. Infection rates varied with depth and reached up to 20.5% of living cells at 10 m (95% confidence interval 17.5–23.9%) and 40% of empty frustules at the surface (95% confidence interval 24.6–57.7%) during bloom conditions. These findings provide quantitative evidence that an oomycete parasite can reach high infection levels in a coastal diatom bloom, and suggest that oomycetes, a previously underappreciated group of parasites, may affect diatom population dynamics and the fate of diatom-derived organic matter in marine ecosystems.

title: ”Bertumbuh Bersama Virus”: Dinamika Resiliensi Pada Emerging Adulthood Dengan HIV Perinatal
abstractText: Individu dengan HIV perinatal yang memasuki fase emerging adulthood menghadapi benturan kompleks antara tuntutan transisi menuju kemandirian dan beban psikososial dari penyakit kronis seumur hidup. Namun, sebagian individu mampu menunjukkan resiliensi dalam menghadapi risiko kesehatan mental dan kesulitan beradaptasi. Tujuan penelitian ini adalah untuk memahami dinamika resiliensi pada emerging adulthood dengan HIV perinatal. Penelitian ini menggunakan pendekatan kualitatif dengan desain fenomenologi. Partisipan terdiri dari dua orang emerging adulthood yang hidup dengan HIV Perinatal yang dipilih melalui teknik purposive sampling. Data dikumpulkan melalui wawancara mendalam dan dianalisis menggunakan Descriptive Phenomenological Analysis (DPA). Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa resiliensi pada emerging adulthood dengan HIV perinatal merupakan proses yang dinamis, dimulai dari pengalaman mengetahui status HIV, menghadapi berbagai tantangan kehidupan, hingga mampu menerima kondisi dan membangun harapan terhadap masa depan. Dinamika tersebut dipengaruhi oleh faktor-faktor yang mendukung resiliensi, yaitu dukungan sosial, efikasi diri, komunitas sesama ODHIV (Orang dengan HIV), spiritualitas, dan penerimaan diri.

Dietary Inclusion of Mondia whitei Root Powder for Male Oreochromis shiranus
abstractText: Most extensive and semi-intensive fish farmers in Malawi are adopting formulating feed on-farm to reduce feed costs. To improve aquafeed quality, research on environmentally friendly and cost-effective feed additives has increased. Therefore, this study assessed the effect of incorporating Mondia whitei root powder as an aromatic feed additive on the proximate composition and palatability of feed in male Oreochromis shiranus to improve feed effectiveness. The morphological characteristics and market acceptability of experimental fish were also assessed. A completely randomized design was used with five dietary treatments of M. whitei inclusion (0, 10, 20, 30, and 40%) for male O. shiranus (experimental mean initial body weight: 80 g). Proximate composition (AOAC methods) was used to determine the nutrient profile of M. whitei root powder and experimental diets. Feed palatability was assessed through video-based observation of fish feeding behavior and quantification of uneaten feed following air-drying. Fish morphological characteristics and market acceptability were assessed through consumer feedback. One-way analysis of variance (ANOVA) at the 5% significance level was used for data analysis. The polynomial trend analysis assessed the potential dose-dependent responses of Mondia whitei inclusion levels. Proximate composition had significant differences for crude protein and fat among diets (p < 0.001), and a significant difference (p < 0.05) in feed palatability was also observed across all treatments. The 20% inclusion diet showed the highest palatability, indicated by a shorter latency time (20 min). Fish growth was comparable across treatments, with no significant differences in percentage weight gain and specific growth rate (SGR, %/day) (p > 0.05). In addition, there was no significant linear or quadratic relationship between the inclusion level of Mondia whitei and SGR (p > 0.05) across treatments, indicating that Mondia whitei inclusion did not negatively influence fish growth performance. The condition factor (K) values were comparable across treatments, suggesting normal physiological conditions and growth. No significant changes in morphological appearance, texture, and color appeal were observed (p > 0.05), with the consumer feedback rating all groups as acceptable and marketable. Therefore, Mondia whitei root powder inclusion in male Oreochromis shiranus diets improved the nutritional profile and feed palatability. It did so without impairing the fish's morphological characteristics or growth performance, showing its potential as a reliable phytogenic additive in formulated fish feed. Key words: Mondia whitei, herbs, feed palatability, Oreochromis shiranus, Aquaculture nutrition, tilapia

title: A dual-anchoring mechanism for hemimethylated CG-guided histone ubiquitylation
abstractText: Abstract Maintenance of plant CG DNA methylation requires VARIANT IN METHYLATION (VIM) proteins, a family of E3 ligases that couple hemimethylated CG (hemiCG) with histone ubiquitylation to regulate MET1-mediated DNA methylation. How the hemiCG readout guides VIM proteins for histone ubiquitylation remains unclear. Here we report structure-function characterization of VIM1-mediated histone ubiquitylation, revealing the N-terminal tails of H3 and H4 as the VIM1 substrates. The structures of VIM1 complexed with hemiCG-containing nucleosome and/or E2 UBC11 reveal that VIM1 is positioned over the nucleosome disk surface, with the RING2 and SRA domains anchored to the H2A-H2B acidic patch and linker hemiCG site, respectively, and the RING1 domain mediating UBC11 loading. The RING2-mediated anchoring helps position RING1 near the H3/H4 tails for substrate access, while the SRA-mediated anchoring antagonizes an autoinhibitory state. Together, such dual nucleosome anchoring by RING2-SRA mechanistically links the position-varying hemiCG mark to persistent, yet context-dependent H3/H4 ubiquitylation.

title: Hubungan Tingkat Kedewasaan Dengan Penerimaan Metode Pembelajaran Andragogi Pada Mahasiswa
abstractText: Penelitian ini menilai hubungan antara tingkat kedewasaan mahasiswa dengan penerimaan metode pembelajaran andragogi, serta mengidentifikasi karakteristik kedewasaan yang paling berkontribusi. Penelitian kuantitatif ini melibatkan 85 mahasiswa Bisnis Kreatif Universitas Indonesia angkatan 2023 yang dipilih melalui purposive sampling, dianalisis menggunakan uji korelasi Pearson dan regresi linear berganda. Hasil uji korelasi menunjukkan hubungan positif dengan kekuatan moderat antara kedewasaan dan penerimaan andragogi (r = .473; p < .001). Dari tujuh karakteristik kedewasaan yang diuji, hanya clear goals and efficient work-habits yang berkontribusi signifikan terhadap penerimaan andragogi (β = .291; p = .013), sementara enam karakteristik lainnya tidak signifikan (p > .05). Temuan ini mengindikasikan asosiasi positif antara kedewasaan dan penerimaan andragogi, namun belum menetapkan ambang kedewasaan minimum yang dibutuhkan, sehingga klaim kecukupan kedewasaan perlu dimaknai secara hati-hati. Penerapan metode pembelajaran andragogi yang konsisten dan reflektif dapat dipertimbangkan untuk menguatkan karakteristik kedewasaan yang belum signifikan, meskipun efektivitasnya belum diuji.

Comparing ultrasonography and coelioscopy for sex identification in immature agile frogs (Rana dalmatina)
abstractText: Abstract Accurate sex identification is essential for animal research, veterinary practice, husbandry and conservation programs, yet it remains challenging in many amphibians because external sexual dimorphism is often weak or absent before sexual maturity. Ultrasonography has been proposed as a non-invasive alternative to more invasive procedures, but its utility for sex identification in juvenile frogs remains untested. This study evaluated the feasibility and reliability of high-frequency ultrasonography (HF-US) for gonadal sex identification in immature agile frogs ( Rana dalmatina ). A total of 101 HF-US examinations were performed on captive-reared froglets, originating from eggs collected from wild populations, with a body length of 4–5 cm. Sex assignments were validated using coelioscopy and genotypic sexing. HF-US produced an ambiguous result in 23% of examinations related to problems such as intestinal gas or ingesta. Among examinations where an unambiguous sex was assigned, overall accuracy was 56.4%, being higher in females (65.4%) than in males (38.5%). Ultrasonographic examinations were substantially faster (ca. 2 min on average) than coelioscopic procedures (ca. 30 min on average). Complications occurred only after coelioscopy, including postoperative wound dehiscence in six individuals and two deaths, mostly within one month after the procedure, during the two autumn months preceding winter hibernation. However, in one female, the healed incision reopened four months later during oviposition in the following spring. Altogether, HF-US provides an accessible, rapid and non-invasive approach for gonad examination; however, its high error rate in identifying immature gonads, particularly testes, is insufficient for reliable phenotypic sex identification in juvenile agile frogs. Coelioscopy provides substantially greater diagnostic certainty, but this advantage must be weighed against its non-zero invasiveness and associated animal-welfare risks. Therefore, we recommend further testing of HF-US, especially when validated non-invasive alternatives are not available, to explore if training with the species and age classes in question could ensure reliable sex identification by this method.
